content.text:
## Setup listo ✅

- **Identidad local**: `Felipe Sabogal <100255652+FelipeSuarez25@users.noreply.github.com>`. No toqué la configuración global.
- **`.claude/settings.json`** con `GH_CONFIG_DIR=/Users/cristiansabogal/.config/gh-felipe`. Comprobé que esa configuración está logueada como **FelipeSuarez25**.
- **Credential helper local**: primero un helper vacío, que anula el `osxkeychain` heredado del gitconfig del sistema. Después `GH_CONFIG_DIR=… /opt/homebrew/bin/gh auth git-credential`. El remote es HTTPS, sin SSH.
- **Repo** `FelipeSuarez25/multicountry-car-insurance` creado como **PRIVATE**.
- **Commit inicial** `674470e` (`.gitignore` + `.claude/settings.json`) subido con push. Según la API de GitHub, el autor es **Felipe Sabogal** con login `FelipeSuarez25`.

Leí el PDF completo (9 páginas). Lo que más pesa en la nota: el 65 % es el flujo agéntico, y piden evidencia explícita de que **el humano corrigió al agente**. Por eso la propuesta pone los puntos de control y su registro en el centro.

---

## 1. Estructura del repo

```
├── CLAUDE.md              # Imports @AGENTS.md + Claude-specific orchestration rules
├── AGENTS.md              # Tool-agnostic conventions (single source, no duplication)
├── FLOW.md                # Step table + Mermaid diagram + the 3 reflection questions
├── README.md              # Run instructions, unmet requirements, tool justification
├── docker-compose.yml     # strapi + frontend (+ e2e profile)
├── .env.example           # Fictitious values only
├── .github/pull_request_template.md   # Traceability matrix per PR
├── .claude/
│   ├── settings.json      # env + permissions + hooks (block .env reads, force-push)
│   ├── agents/            # Subagent definitions
│   └── skills/            # Own skills + approved external ones (with ORIGIN.md)
├── specs/US-01/  story.md (verbatim, human) · spec.md · tasks.md
├── specs/US-02/ …  specs/US-03/ …
├── adr/                   # 0001-multi-country-content-strategy.md, …
├── reviews/               # US-01-review-R1.md, …
├── logs/sessions/         # Unedited session exports
├── scripts/trace.sh       # Deterministic traceability matrix (no AI)
├── frontend/              # Angular 21, Vitest (unit), Playwright (e2e)
└── backend/               # Strapi 5, seed CO/CL in bootstrap
```

Añado tres cosas que no estaban en tu lista: `logs/`, `scripts/trace.sh` y la plantilla de PR.

## 2. Subagentes

La sesión principal hace de **orquestador** y sigue FLOW.md. En Claude Code un subagente no puede lanzar otros subagentes, así que la coordinación queda en la sesión principal.

| Agente | Responsabilidad | Herramientas | Entrada → Salida |
|---|---|---|---|
| `spec-writer` | Convierte la US en spec verificable: detecta huecos, numera BR/AC y abre preguntas para el humano | Read, Grep, Glob, Write (solo `specs/`) | `story.md` → `spec.md`, `tasks.md` |
| `architect` | Detecta decisiones, escribe ADRs con alternativas reales y valida que la spec no choque con ADRs vigentes | Read, Grep, Glob, Write (solo `adr/`), WebFetch (docs oficiales) | `spec.md` → `adr/NNNN-*.md` (Proposed) |
| `test-engineer` | Escribe los tests **desde la spec, antes del código** (unit + e2e), sin leer la implementación primero | Read, Write, Edit, Bash (test runners) | `spec.md` → `*.spec.ts`, `e2e/*.spec.ts` |
| `strapi-developer` | Content types, seed CO/CL, permisos del rol público, bootstrap | Read, Write, Edit, Bash (dentro de `backend/`) | spec + ADR + tasks → `backend/**` |
| `angular-developer` | Wizard, formulario dinámico, estado con signals, a11y y responsive | Read, Write, Edit, Bash (dentro de `frontend/`) | spec + ADR + tasks + tests rojos → `frontend/**` |
| `code-reviewer` | Revisión independiente contra la spec, la checklist y los ADRs. **No edita código** | Read, Grep, Glob, Bash (solo lint/test/build), Write (solo `reviews/`) | diff + spec → `reviews/US-0X-review-RN.md` |

El tester está separado de los desarrolladores a propósito: si quien implementa escribe sus propios tests, tiende a validar lo que hizo y no lo que pide la spec.

## 3. Skills

Sobre tu propuesta: mantengo las 5 y sugiero 2 más.

| Skill | Valor | Usada por |
|---|---|---|
| `sdd-spec` ✔ | Plantilla de spec, checklist de detección de huecos y formato de IDs | spec-writer |
| `adr-madr` ✔ | Plantilla MADR y criterio de cuándo merece ADR. Es delgada, pero barata | architect |
| `strapi-content-modeling` ✔ | Strapi 5: `documentId`, draft & publish, relación de país, permisos mínimos, seed idempotente | strapi-dev, architect |
| `dynamic-form-fields` ✔ | Contrato campo de Strapi → validadores tipados, reglas de edad y año, mapeo de errores | angular-dev, test-engineer |
| `review-checklist` ✔ | Severidades, checklist (seguridad, a11y, multi-país, Angular moderno), formato de hallazgo | code-reviewer |
| **`test-from-spec`** ➕ | Cada AC se convierte en un test nombrado con su ID; convenciones de Vitest y Playwright | test-engineer |
| **`session-handoff`** ➕ | Procedimiento de cierre y retomada: actualizar `tasks.md`, exportar el log y dejar la "próxima acción" | orquestador |

**Externas**: todavía no evalúo ninguna. Cuando apruebes, busco candidatas de Angular y de diseño en skills.sh, las leo y te entrego una tabla "sirve / choca" contra Angular 21+, standalone, signals, `@if/@for` y sin NgModules. Las globales que ya tienes instaladas (frontend-design, impeccable, etc.) no las uso, como pediste.

## 4. Flujo y puntos de control humanos

```
H0 Intake (humano, sin IA) → 1 Spec → [HC1] → 2 ADRs → [HC2] → 3 Tests rojos
→ 4 Implementación → 5 Gate automático → 6 Review → 7 Fixes → [HC3 PR] → Ready for QA
```

| Punto de control | Qué revisas | Apruebas si… | Si rechazas… |
|---|---|---|---|
| **HC1 Spec** | `spec.md` | Cada AC tiene ID y es verificable, las preguntas abiertas están resueltas por ti, el fuera de alcance es explícito y no hay contradicción con ADRs | Anotas el motivo en la sección *Review log* de la spec; el spec-writer reescribe y queda la versión anterior en git |
| **HC2 ADR** | `adr/*.md` | Hay ≥2 alternativas reales, consecutivas y justificación; el estado pasa a *Accepted* **solo si tú lo cambias** | Eliges otra alternativa o pasa a *Rejected* (se conserva); el architect reescribe |
| **Gate auto** (sin humano) | lint, typecheck, unit, e2e, build, smoke de `docker compose` | Todo verde | Vuelve al desarrollador; tras 3 vueltas fallidas, escala al humano |
| **HC3 PR** | PR + review report + QA manual (CO y CL, solo teclado, móvil) | 0 hallazgos blocker/major abiertos, matriz de trazabilidad completa, todos los AC verificados a mano | Comentas en el PR y vuelve al paso 4; **el merge lo haces tú** |

Lo que **no** hace la IA: el intake de la US, aceptar ADRs, el merge, la prueba manual de teclado y a11y, la elección de skills externas y cualquier manejo de secretos.

## 5. Trazabilidad

- **IDs**: `US-01` · `US-01-BR-03` (regla) · `US-01-AC-02` (escenario) · `US-01-Q-01` (hueco o pregunta) · `US-01-T-04` (tarea) · `ADR-0001` · `US-01-R1-F03` (review ronda 1, hallazgo 3).
- **Rama**: `feat/us-01-dynamic-form`.
- **Commit**: Conventional Commits con trailers, por ejemplo `feat(form): …`, luego `Refs: US-01-AC-02, ADR-0001`, y en los fixes `Resolves: US-01-R1-F03`.
- **Tests**: `describe('US-01-AC-02 field validation', …)`.
- **Review**: cada hallazgo tiene una tabla con el SHA del commit que lo resolvió y su estado.
- **PR**: la plantilla incluye la matriz AC → archivos → test → estado. `scripts/trace.sh US-01` la genera con grep, sin IA, para comprobar que nadie la inventó.

## 6. Cómo se retoma entre sesiones

- **`specs/US-0X/tasks.md`**: tareas con estado, el punto de control actual, bloqueos y una línea **"Next action"**. CLAUDE.md obliga a actualizarlo al cerrar cada paso.
- **Al iniciar una sesión**: leer CLAUDE.md → `tasks.md` de la HU activa → continuar desde "Next action". Todo el estado vive en el repo, sin memoria externa.
- **Logs**: al cerrar cada sesión se copia el JSONL crudo de Claude Code y el `/export` a `logs/sessions/AAAA-MM-DD-<id>.*`, sin editar. Antes del commit, un escaneo de secretos (gitleaks o grep); si encuentra algo, no se commitea y se avisa.

# Angular Skills

The Angular skills are designed to help coding agents create applications aligned with the latest versions of Angular, best practices, new features and manage Angular applications effectively. These skills provide architectural guidance, generate idiomatic Angular code, and help scaffold new projects using modern best practices.

## Available Skills

- **`angular-developer`**: Generates Angular code and provides architectural guidance. Useful for creating components, services, HTTP communication, or obtaining best practices on reactivity (signals, linkedSignal, resource, httpResource), queries and content projection, forms, dependency injection, routing, SSR, accessibility (ARIA), animations, styling, testing, or CLI tooling.
- **`angular-new-app`**: Creates a new Angular app using the Angular CLI. Provides important guidelines for effectively setting up and structuring a modern Angular application.

## Using Agent Skills

Agent Skills are designed to be used with agentic coding tools like [Gemini CLI](https://geminicli.com/docs/cli/skills/), [Antigravity](https://antigravity.google/docs/skills) and more. Activating a skill loads the specific instructions and resources needed for that task.

To use these skills in your own environment you may follow the instructions for your specific tool or use a community tool like [skills.sh](https://skills.sh/).

```bash
npx skills add https://github.com/angular/skills
```

## Contributions

We welcome contributions to the Angular agent skills. If you would like to contribute to the skills, please make the updates directly in `angular/angular` repository, and to that repository will be output here as a part of our infrastructure setup.

### Feedback & Issues

If you encounter a bug, have feedback, or want to suggest an improvement to the skills, please file an issue in the [angular/angular](https://github.com/angular/angular/issues/new?template=3-docs-bug.yaml) issue tracker. Providing detailed context will help us address your feedback effectively.

### Features & Changes (Pull Requests)

We also accept pull requests for new features, updates, or bug fixes for the skills:

1. Make your changes within the `skills/dev-skills/` directory.
2. Follow the standard Angular [Commit Guidelines](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/main/contributing-docs/commit-message-guidelines.md) and [Coding Standards](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/main/contributing-docs/coding-standards.md).
3. Submit a Pull Request to the main `angular/angular` repository.

# Angular Developer Guidelines

1. Always analyze the project's Angular version before providing guidance, as best practices and available features can vary significantly between versions. If creating a new project with Angular CLI, do not specify a version unless prompted by the user.

2. When generating code, follow Angular's style guide and best practices for maintainability and performance. Use the Angular CLI for scaffolding components, services, directives, pipes, and routes to ensure consistency.

3. Once you finish generating code, run `ng build` to ensure there are no build errors. If there are errors, analyze the error messages and fix them before proceeding. Do not skip this step, as it is critical for ensuring the generated code is correct and functional.

## Creating New Projects

If no guidelines are provided by the user, here are some default rules to follow when creating a new Angular project:

1. Use the latest stable version of Angular unless the user specifies otherwise.
2. Use Signal Forms for form management in new projects (stable in Angular v22 and newer) [Find out more](references/signal-forms.md).

**Execution Rules for `ng new`:**
When asked to create a new Angular project, you must determine the correct execution command by following these strict steps:

**Step 1: Check for an explicit user version.**

- **IF** the user requests a specific version (e.g., Angular 15), bypass local installations and strictly use `npx`.
- **Command:** `npx @angular/cli@<requested_version> new <project-name>`

**Step 2: Check for an existing Angular installation.**

- **IF** no specific version is requested, run `ng version` in the terminal to check if the Angular CLI is already installed on the system.
- **IF** the command succeeds and returns an installed version, use the local/global installation directly.
- **Command:** `ng new <project-name>`

**Step 3: Fallback to Latest.**

- **IF** no specific version is requested AND the `ng version` command fails (indicating no Angular installation exists), you must use `npx` to fetch the latest version.
- **Command:** `npx @angular/cli@latest new <project-name>`

## Components

When working with Angular components, consult the following references based on the task:

- **Fundamentals**: Anatomy, metadata, core concepts, self-closing tags, and template control flow (@if, @for, @switch). Read [components.md](references/components.md)
- **Inputs**: Signal-based inputs, transforms, and model inputs. Read [inputs.md](references/inputs.md)
- **Outputs**: Signal-based outputs and custom event best practices. Read [outputs.md](references/outputs.md)
- **Host Elements**: Host bindings and attribute injection. Read [host-elements.md](references/host-elements.md)
- **Naming Conventions**: Modern Angular v20+ naming style ("Intent over Role") for files, components, services, directives, pipes, and models. Read [naming-conventions.md](references/naming-conventions.md)
- **Queries and Content Projection**: Signal-based view and content queries (viewChild, viewChildren, contentChild, contentChildren) and content projection with `<ng-content>` slots and fallback content. Read [queries-and-projection.md](references/queries-and-projection.md)
- **Deferrable Views**: Lazy loading, code splitting, triggers, prefetching, loading states, SSR, and layout stability with `@defer`. Read [deferrable-views.md](references/deferrable-views.md)
- **Error Boundaries**: Catching render and change detection errors in a template subtree with `@boundary`/`@error`, retrying with `$reset`. Read [error-boundary.md](references/error-boundary.md)

**Template expressions**: Avoid expensive work in templates (e.g. building arrays or objects, filtering, sorting), since it re-runs on every change detection cycle. Reading signals (`count()`) and cheap calls are fine. Derive other values with `computed()`, a pure pipe, or a child component. See [Avoiding expensive work in templates](references/components.md#avoiding-expensive-work-in-templates).

If you require deeper documentation not found in the references above, read the documentation at `https://angular.dev/guide/components`.

## Reactivity and Data Management

When managing state and data reactivity, use Angular Signals and consult the following references:

- **Signals Overview**: Core signal concepts (`signal`, `computed`), reactive contexts, and `untracked`. Read [signals-overview.md](references/signals-overview.md)
- **Dependent State (`linkedSignal`)**: Creating writable state linked to source signals. Read [linked-signal.md](references/linked-signal.md)
- **Async Reactivity (`resource`)**: Fetching asynchronous data directly into signal state. Read [resource.md](references/resource.md)
- **Side Effects (`effect`)**: Logging, third-party DOM manipulation (`afterRenderEffect`), and when NOT to use effects. Read [effects.md](references/effects.md)

## HTTP Communication

When communicating with backend services, use Angular HTTP APIs and consult the following reference:

- **HTTP Client and Resources**: `provideHttpClient`, `HttpClient`, interceptors, and `httpResource`. Read [http-client.md](references/http-client.md)

## Forms

In most cases for new apps, **prefer signal forms**. When making a forms decision, analyze the project and consider the following guidelines:

- If the application is using v22 or newer and this is a new form, **prefer Signal Forms**.
- For older applications or when working with existing forms, use the appropriate form type that matches the applications current form strategy.

- **Signal Forms**: Use signals for form state management. Read [signal-forms.md](references/signal-forms.md)
- **Template-driven forms**: Use for simple forms. Read [template-driven-forms.md](references/template-driven-forms.md)
- **Reactive forms**: Use for complex forms. Read [reactive-forms.md](references/reactive-forms.md)

## Dependency Injection

When implementing dependency injection in Angular, follow these guidelines:

- **Fundamentals**: Overview of Dependency Injection, services, and the `inject()` function. Read [di-fundamentals.md](references/di-fundamentals.md)
- **Creating and Using Services**: Creating services, the `providedIn: 'root'` option, and injecting into components or other services. Read [creating-services.md](references/creating-services.md)

# Angular Skills

The Angular skills are designed to help coding agents create applications aligned with the latest versions of Angular, best practices, new features and manage Angular applications effectively. These skills provide architectural guidance, generate idiomatic Angular code, and help scaffold new projects using modern best practices.

## Available Skills

- **`angular-developer`**: Generates Angular code and provides architectural guidance. Useful for creating components, services, HTTP communication, or obtaining best practices on reactivity (signals, linkedSignal, resource, httpResource), queries and content projection, forms, dependency injection, routing, SSR, accessibility (ARIA), animations, styling, testing, or CLI tooling.
- **`angular-new-app`**: Creates a new Angular app using the Angular CLI. Provides important guidelines for effectively setting up and structuring a modern Angular application.

## Using Agent Skills

Agent Skills are designed to be used with agentic coding tools like [Gemini CLI](https://geminicli.com/docs/cli/skills/), [Antigravity](https://antigravity.google/docs/skills) and more. Activating a skill loads the specific instructions and resources needed for that task.

To use these skills in your own environment you may follow the instructions for your specific tool or use a community tool like [skills.sh](https://skills.sh/).

```bash
npx skills add https://github.com/angular/skills
```

## Contributions

We welcome contributions to the Angular agent skills. If you would like to contribute to the skills, please make the updates directly in `angular/angular` repository, and to that repository will be output here as a part of our infrastructure setup.

### Feedback & Issues

If you encounter a bug, have feedback, or want to suggest an improvement to the skills, please file an issue in the [angular/angular](https://github.com/angular/angular/issues/new?template=3-docs-bug.yaml) issue tracker. Providing detailed context will help us address your feedback effectively.

### Features & Changes (Pull Requests)

We also accept pull requests for new features, updates, or bug fixes for the skills:

1. Make your changes within the `skills/dev-skills/` directory.
2. Follow the standard Angular [Commit Guidelines](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/main/contributing-docs/commit-message-guidelines.md) and [Coding Standards](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/main/contributing-docs/coding-standards.md).
3. Submit a Pull Request to the main `angular/angular` repository.

# Angular Developer Guidelines

1. Always analyze the project's Angular version before providing guidance, as best practices and available features can vary significantly between versions. If creating a new project with Angular CLI, do not specify a version unless prompted by the user.

2. When generating code, follow Angular's style guide and best practices for maintainability and performance. Use the Angular CLI for scaffolding components, services, directives, pipes, and routes to ensure consistency.

3. Once you finish generating code, run `ng build` to ensure there are no build errors. If there are errors, analyze the error messages and fix them before proceeding. Do not skip this step, as it is critical for ensuring the generated code is correct and functional.

## Creating New Projects

If no guidelines are provided by the user, here are some default rules to follow when creating a new Angular project:

1. Use the latest stable version of Angular unless the user specifies otherwise.
2. Use Signal Forms for form management in new projects (stable in Angular v22 and newer) [Find out more](references/signal-forms.md).

**Execution Rules for `ng new`:**
When asked to create a new Angular project, you must determine the correct execution command by following these strict steps:

**Step 1: Check for an explicit user version.**

- **IF** the user requests a specific version (e.g., Angular 15), bypass local installations and strictly use `npx`.
- **Command:** `npx @angular/cli@<requested_version> new <project-name>`

**Step 2: Check for an existing Angular installation.**

- **IF** no specific version is requested, run `ng version` in the terminal to check if the Angular CLI is already installed on the system.
- **IF** the command succeeds and returns an installed version, use the local/global installation directly.
- **Command:** `ng new <project-name>`

**Step 3: Fallback to Latest.**

- **IF** no specific version is requested AND the `ng version` command fails (indicating no Angular installation exists), you must use `npx` to fetch the latest version.
- **Command:** `npx @angular/cli@latest new <project-name>`

**Template expressions**: Avoid expensive work in templates (e.g. building arrays or objects, filtering, sorting), since it re-runs on every change detection cycle. Reading signals (`count()`) and cheap calls are fine. Derive other values with `computed()`, a pure pipe, or a child component. # Signal Forms

Signal Forms are the recommended approach for handling forms in modern Angular applications (v21+). They provide a reactive, type-safe, and model-driven way to manage form state using Angular Signals.

**CRITICAL**: You MUST use Angular's new Signal Forms API for all form-related functionality. Do NOT use null as a value or type of any fields.

## Imports

You can import the following from `@angular/forms/signals`:

```ts
import {
  form,
  FormField,
  submit,
  // Rules for field state
  disabled,
  hidden,
  readonly,
  debounce,
  // Schema helpers
  applyWhen,
  applyEach,
  schema,
  // Custom validation
  validate,
  validateHttp,
  validateStandardSchema,
  // Metadata
  metadata,
} from '@angular/forms/signals';
```

## Creating a Form

Use the `form()` function with a Signal model. The structure of the form is derived directly from the model.

```ts
import {Component, signal} from '@angular/core';
import {form, FormField} from '@angular/forms/signals';

@Component({
  // ...
  imports: [FormField],
})
export class Example {
  // 1. Define your model with initial values (avoid undefined)
  protected readonly userModel = signal({
    name: '', // CRITICAL: NEVER use null or undefined as initial values
    email: '',
    age: 0, // Use 0 for numbers, NOT null
    address: {
      street: '',
      city: '',
    },
    hobbies: [] as string[], // Use [] for arrays, NOT null
  });

  // WRONG - DO NOT DO THIS:
  // badModel = signal({

## Reactive Forms

**Do NOT import** `FormControl`, `FormGroup`, `FormArray`, or `FormBuilder` from `@angular/forms`. Signal Forms replace these concepts entirely.
Signal forms does NOT have a builder.

## Accessing State

Each field in the form is a function that returns its state.

```ts
// Access the field by calling it
const emailState = this.userForm.email();

// Value (WritableSignal)
const value = this.userForm().value();

// Validation State (Signals)
const isValid = this.userForm().valid();
const isInvalid = this.userForm().invalid();
const errors = this.userForm().errors(); // Array of errors
const error = this.userForm().getError('...'); // Single error, by error `kind`
const isPending = this.userForm().pending(); // Async validation pending

// Interaction State (Signals)
const isTouched = this.userForm().touched();
const isDirty = this.userForm().dirty();

// Availability State (Signals)
const isDisabled = this.userForm().disabled();
const isHidden = this.userForm().hidden();
const isReadonly = this.userForm().readonly();
```

IMPORTANT!: Make sure to call the field to get it state.

```ts
form().invalid()
form.field().dirty()
form.field.subfield().touched()
form.a.b.c.d().value()
form.address.ssn().pending()
form().reset()

// The only exception is length:
form.children.length
form.length // NOTE: no parenthesis!
form.client.addresses.length  // No "()"

@for (income of form.addresses; track $index) {/**/}
```

## Submitting

Use the `submit()` function. It automatically marks all fields as touched before running the action.

**CRITICAL**: The callback to `submit()` MUST be `async` and MUST return a Promise.

```ts
import { submit } from '@angular/forms/signals';

// CORRECT - async callback
onSubmit() {
  submit(this.userForm, async () => {
    // This only runs if the form is valid
    await this.apiService.save(this.userModel());
    console.log('Saved!');
  });
}

// WRONG - missing async keyword
onSubmit() {
  submit(this.userForm, () => {  // ERROR: must be async
    console.log('Saved!');
  });
}
```

## Handling Errors

`field().errors()` returns the errors array of ValidationError:

```ts
interface ValidationError {
  readonly kind: string;
  readonly message?: string;
}
```

`field().getError('...')` returns a single ValidationError by its `kind`.

Do _NOT_ return null from validators.
When there are no errors, return undefined

## Reactive Forms

**Do NOT import** `FormControl`, `FormGroup`, `FormArray`, or `FormBuilder` from `@angular/forms`. Signal Forms replace these concepts entirely.
Signal forms does NOT have a builder.

## Accessing State

Each field in the form is a function that returns its state.

```ts
// Access the field by calling it
const emailState = this.userForm.email();

// Value (WritableSignal)
const value = this.userForm().value();

// Validation State (Signals)
const isValid = this.userForm().valid();
const isInvalid = this.userForm().invalid();
const errors = this.userForm().errors(); // Array of errors
const error = this.userForm().getError('...'); // Single error, by error `kind`
const isPending = this.userForm().pending(); // Async validation pending

// Interaction State (Signals)
const isTouched = this.userForm().touched();
const isDirty = this.userForm().dirty();

// Availability State (Signals)
const isDisabled = this.userForm().disabled();
const isHidden = this.userForm().hidden();
const isReadonly = this.userForm().readonly();
```

IMPORTANT!: Make sure to call the field to get it state.

```ts
form().invalid()
form.field().dirty()
form.field.subfield().touched()
form.a.b.c.d().value()
form.address.ssn().pending()
form().reset()

// The only exception is length:
form.children.length
form.length // NOTE: no parenthesis!
form.client.addresses.length  // No "()"

@for (income of form.addresses; track $index) {/**/}
```

## Submitting

Use the `submit()` function. It automatically marks all fields as touched before running the action.

**CRITICAL**: The callback to `submit()` MUST be `async` and MUST return a Promise.

```ts
import { submit } from '@angular/forms/signals';

// CORRECT - async callback
onSubmit() {
  submit(this.userForm, async () => {
    // This only runs if the form is valid
    await this.apiService.save(this.userModel());
    console.log('Saved!');
  });
}

// WRONG - missing async keyword
onSubmit() {
  submit(this.userForm, () => {  // ERROR: must be async
    console.log('Saved!');
  });
}
```

## Handling Errors

`field().errors()` returns the errors array of ValidationError:

```ts
interface ValidationError {
  readonly kind: string;
  readonly message?: string;
}
```

`field().getError('...')` returns a single ValidationError by its `kind`.

Do _NOT_ return null from validators.
When there are no errors, return undefined

# Angular Naming Conventions (Angular v20+ Style Guide)

This skill enforces Angular naming conventions for components, services, directives, pipes, and models. While it promotes the modern **"Intent over Role"** philosophy introduced in Angular v20, **it must respect existing project configurations first**.

---

## Core Principles

1. **Prioritize Existing Conventions**: Before generating or refactoring files, check the existing project files, `angular.json` configuration, and ESLint rules. **Do not force suffixless naming on projects that rely on standard suffixes.**
2. **Remove Role Suffixes (Modern Projects Only)**: In projects configured for "Intent over Role" or newly bootstrapped v20+ projects, filenames no longer include functional extensions like `.component.ts`, `.service.ts`, or `.directive.ts`. Corresponding TypeScript classes drop suffixes like `Component`, `Service`, or `Directive`.
3. **Intent/Purpose-Based Naming**: When suffixless naming is active, name files and classes based on their specific domain, responsibility, or business purpose (e.g., `-data`, `-store`, `-api`, or `-formatter`).
4. **Folder Location as Context**: Lean on folder hierarchy (`core/`, `features/`, `shared/`) and IDE capabilities to identify the technical role of files, rather than encoding that context within the file name.
5. **Interface/Model Exception**: Interfaces and data models still retain the `.model.ts` suffix to clearly declare type contracts.

---

## Recommended Project Structure & Naming Rules

### 1. File/Identifier Matching & Consistency

- **Hyphens in Filenames**: Continue using kebab-case (hyphens) to separate words in filenames (e.g., `product-list.ts`).
- **Identifier Matching**: Filenames must align directly with the primary TypeScript class/identifier (e.g., `product-list.ts` contains `class ProductList`).
- **Unified Filenames**: If using split template or style files, keep names identical to the main TypeScript file:
  - `product-list.ts`
  - `product-list.html`
  - `product-list.css`
- **Test Files**: Continue to use the same base name with the `.spec.ts` suffix (e.g., `product-list.spec.ts` for `product-list.ts`).

### 2. Core Directory (Application Foundation)

Houses singleton services, global state, and system-wide models.

- **Services (Logic/State)**:
  - _Old_: `auth.service.ts` (Class: `AuthService`)
  - _New_: `auth.ts` (Class: `AuthService`)
  - _Alternative (Intent-specific)_: Use descriptive domain-purpose suffixes like `[domain]-data.ts`, `[domain]-store.ts`, or `[domain]-data-client.ts` (e.g., `auth-data.ts` / `AuthData`, `user-data-client.ts` / `UserDataClient`).
- **Models**: Retain the `.model.ts` suffix for data shapes.
  - _Example_: `user.model.ts` (Interface: `User`)

# Third-party skill evaluations

Every external skill is evaluated **before** installation. Each one is read from its
source repository (not from a registry summary) and checked against the project
requirements and our own conventions (`CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `.claude/skills/`).
Only a human can approve an installation. Approved skills are recorded in
`.claude/skills/THIRD_PARTY.md`.

Verdict scale: **ADOPT** · **ADOPT WITH ADJUSTMENTS** · **REJECT**.

---

## EVAL-001 — `angular-developer` from angular/skills

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Evaluation date | 2026-11-20 |
| Evaluated by | Claude Code (Opus 5.5), main session |
| Source URL | https://github.com/angular/skills (path `angular-developer/`) |
| Evaluated commit | `97c663a02b376a19eccc60f75909f20f15a2c9c1` (2026-11-20 17:10 UTC) |
| Upstream origin | Generated from `angular/angular` → `skills/dev-skills/`, upstream commit `8b15295e8c7f1543d41dadb5955279702be52c16` (see `BUILD_INFO`) |
| Author | Google LLC / Angular team (`metadata.author: Copyright 2026 Google LLC`) |
| Skill version | `1.0` (frontmatter, so it is not useful for pinning; we pin by commit) |
| License | MIT, declared in the SKILL.md frontmatter. The mirror repo has **no LICENSE file** and GitHub reports `license: null`. The upstream `angular/angular` repo is MIT. |
| Status | **Active.** Not archived; synced from `angular/angular` several times a day (last push 2026-11-20). |
| Files read | `SKILL.md` (150 lines) + 44 reference files (5,171 lines). Read in full: `SKILL.md`, `testing-fundamentals.md`, `e2e-testing.md`, `mcp.md`, `reactive-forms.md`, `naming-conventions.md` (core rules), `signal-forms.md` (all key sections). The remaining references were scanned by pattern (see the security section). |

### Criteria reviewed

#### 1. Compatibility with project requirements

Latest stable Angular at evaluation time: **22.3.0** (npm `latest`; `next` = 22.3.0-rc.0).
The assessment requires Angular 21 or later, so 22.x qualifies.

| Requirement | Result | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Angular 21+ / latest stable | ✅ | Targets "latest versions"; tells the agent to detect the project's version first (SKILL.md rule 1). |
| Standalone, no NgModules | ✅ | `components.md`: standalone is the default since v19. `NgModule` appears only in the standalone migration guide and in `TestBed` explanations. |
| Signals | ✅ | `signal`, `computed`, `linkedSignal`, `resource`, `httpResource`, signal inputs, outputs and queries. |
| Built-in control flow `@if/@for` | ✅ | All templates use `@if/@for/@switch`; no `*ngIf/*ngFor` anywhere. |
| Vitest | ✅ | `testing-fundamentals.md` assumes Vitest, zoneless, and an "Act, Wait, Assert" pattern with `await fixture.whenStable()`. `cli.md` still mentions Karma as a possible runner (neutral). |
| Playwright | ⚠️ Neutral | `e2e-testing.md` lists 5 frameworks and suggests `ng add playwright-ng-schematics`, a community package, not an official Angular one. It does not conflict, but it brings no Playwright guidance of its own. |
| Keyboard accessibility | ⚠️ Partial | `angular-aria.md` covers keyboard interaction for complex widgets (listbox, combobox, tabs…). Nothing on wizard focus management, focus on errors or `aria-describedby` for field errors. Our `review-checklist` must still cover this. |

#### 2. Conflicts with our CLAUDE.md and own skills

| # | Rule in the skill | Conflict | Resolution |
|---|---|---|---|
| C1 | `signal-forms.md`: "You MUST use Angular's new Signal Forms API for all form-related functionality" and "Do NOT import FormControl, FormGroup…" | It decides the forms strategy before our ADR does, and it contradicts `SKILL.md`, which allows Reactive Forms for complex or existing forms. | Precedence rule in `CLAUDE.md`: **CLAUDE.md > accepted ADRs > own skills > third-party skills**. The forms ADR decides. |
| C2 | SKILL.md rule 2 / `ng new`: "do not specify a version unless prompted"; falls back to `npx @angular/cli@latest` | Non-reproducible scaffolding. | `CLAUDE.md` pins the CLI version (`npx @angular/cli@22.3.x`). The skill's own Step 1 honours an explicit version. |
| C3 | `mcp.md`: configure the Angular CLI MCP server via `npx -y @angular/cli mcp` | User rule: no external tools; all context lives in the repo. | `CLAUDE.md`: do not configure MCP servers. The file stays unmodified so provenance is preserved, but it is not followed. |
| C4 | SKILL.md: "read the documentation at angular.dev" when the references are not enough | Remote reads; the context should live in the repo. | Read-only reads of `angular.dev` are allowed, but any decision based on them must be written into a spec or ADR. |
| C5 | `naming-conventions.md`: v20+ suffixless naming ("Intent over Role"), but also "respect existing project conventions"; its own examples are inconsistent (`auth.ts` → `class AuthService`) | Ambiguous until we decide. | `CLAUDE.md` states the naming convention explicitly (proposal: v22 CLI defaults, suffixless files). |
| C6 | `e2e-testing.md`: `ng add playwright-ng-schematics` | Pulls in a community dependency. | Playwright setup follows our `test-from-spec` skill (`@playwright/test` directly). The schematic is not used unless a human approves it. |
| C7 | SKILL.md rule 3: run `ng build` after generating code | None. It matches our automated gate. | Keep. |

No conflict with `sdd-spec`, `adr-madr`, `strapi-content-modeling` or `review-checklist`.
`dynamic-form-fields` and `test-from-spec` are **complementary** (see criterion 4).

#### 3. Security: commands, remote content, anything suspicious

- **No scripts, binaries or hooks.** Only Markdown files plus `BUILD_INFO`.
- Commands found: `ng build/test/e2e/add/generate`, `npx @angular/cli@<version> new`,
  `npx @angular/cli@latest new`, `npx -y @angular/cli mcp`. The `npx` calls download npm
  packages when executed; this is covered by C2 and C3.
- External domains: only `angular.dev` (docs), `api.example.com` (examples) and `localhost`.
- No hidden or bidirectional Unicode characters, no base64, no `curl | sh`, no instructions
  aimed at secrets, credentials or files outside the project.
- **Supply-chain note:** the content changes daily and `npx skills add` installs whatever
  is at HEAD, not the evaluated commit. Mitigation: after installation, diff the installed
  files against commit `97c663a`. If they differ, stop and re-evaluate.
- Licensing: MIT requires keeping the copyright notice. Because the mirror has no LICENSE
  file, `THIRD_PARTY.md` must record the notice and point to the upstream license.

#### 4. Value beyond our own skills and CLAUDE.md

| Area | Our coverage | What angular-developer adds |
|---|---|---|
| Signal Forms API (`form`, `[formField]`, `validate`, `applyEach`, `applyWhen`, `submit`, `validateStandardSchema`) | `dynamic-form-fields` covers the Strapi→validator **contract**, not the API | **High.** Up-to-date API reference with a "Common pitfalls" table and a section on recovering from build errors. This is where an LLM is most likely to hallucinate an API that only reached stable in v22. |
| Zoneless, async-first unit testing with Vitest | `test-from-spec` covers AC-ID naming and Gherkin→test mapping | **High.** Correct `whenStable()` patterns; avoids `detectChanges()` anti-patterns. |
| `resource` / `httpResource`, `linkedSignal`, `effect` guidance | Not covered | **Medium-high.** Loading and error states for Strapi calls (graded under "technical quality"). |
| Runtime configuration (`provideAppInitializer`) | Not covered | **Medium.** Relevant because the same build must serve CO and CL and point to Strapi at runtime. |
| Routing, guards, `@defer`, `@boundary` error boundaries | Not covered | **Medium.** Wizard step guards and error isolation. |
| SSR, Tailwind, animations, MCP, deployment | Not needed | None, but harmless because they load on demand. |

#### 5. Signal Forms vs Reactive Forms (input for the forms ADR)

**What the skill says**

- `SKILL.md`: "Use Signal Forms for form management in new projects (stable in Angular v22
  and newer)." Prefer Signal Forms for new forms on v22+. For older apps or existing forms,
  keep the current strategy. Reactive Forms are listed for "complex forms".
- `signal-forms.md`: Signal Forms are "the recommended approach… (v21+)". It **mandates**
  them for all forms and forbids `FormControl/FormGroup/FormBuilder`.
- This is an **internal inconsistency**: "v21+ / MUST" against "v22+ / prefer". We checked
  the official source instead of trusting either statement:

**Verified facts (latest stable 22.3.0)**

- `angular/angular` CHANGELOG, **22.0.0 (2026-06-03)**, forms: commit `7745365910`,
  *"graduate signal forms APIs to public API"*. In v21 they were experimental.
- Published `@angular/forms@22.3.0` typings: all `@angular/forms/signals` APIs are tagged
  `@publicApi 22.0` (one is `22.1`). The only `@experimental` symbol is
  `provideExperimentalWebMcpForms`, which we do not need.
- `@angular/forms/signals-compat` (`@publicApi 22.0`) provides `compatForm` and
  `SignalFormControl` to interoperate with Reactive Forms.
- The schema API we need is exported: `required`, `min`, `max`, `pattern`, `validate`,
  `applyEach`, `applyWhen`, `metadata`, `validateStandardSchema`, `submit`.

**Implications for a Strapi-driven dynamic form (to be weighed in the ADR)**

- ➕ The form structure is derived from a model signal, so a model built at runtime from the
  Strapi field config plus a schema function that loops over the config is a natural fit.
  Custom rules (legal age, vehicle year range) map to `validate()`. Strapi error messages
  map to `ValidationError.message`.
- ➕ Signal-native state (`valid()`, `touched()`, `errors()`) fits a signals-only wizard
  and avoids `toSignal` bridges.
- ➖ The model shape is only known at runtime, so typing degrades to `Record<string, …>`.
  The "typed validations" requirement then depends on a typed **config** contract, not on
  the form type.
- ➖ The skill's rules: no `null` values (use `''`/`0`), no `<select multiple>`, checkboxes
  bind only to booleans, and no `min/max/value` attributes on inputs. "Required number with
  initial value `0`" and empty date fields need a spike to confirm behaviour.
- ➖ It has been stable for only about 5 months. Reactive Forms (`FormRecord`) remain the
  proven path for dynamic forms and are still supported (`ReactiveFormsModule` is imported
  into a standalone component; we author no NgModules).

### Verdict: **ADOPT WITH ADJUSTMENTS**

**Reasons:** it is official, active, MIT, has no executable content, and is aligned with
Angular 22 (standalone, signals, control flow, Vitest, zoneless). Its main value is an
up-to-date Signal Forms and testing reference that our own skills do not provide and that
models tend to get wrong. The conflicts (C1–C6) can all be resolved with precedence and
explicit rules in `CLAUDE.md`, without editing vendored files.

**Required adjustments, if approved:**

1. Install only `angular-developer`, at project scope, and verify that the installed files
   match commit `97c663a` (diff). On mismatch, stop and re-evaluate.
2. Record the source, commit, upstream commit, license and copyright notice in
   `.claude/skills/THIRD_PARTY.md`.
3. Add the precedence rule to `CLAUDE.md` (CLAUDE.md > accepted ADRs > own skills >
   third-party) and the explicit overrides C1–C6.
4. Do not modify vendored files. Overrides live in `CLAUDE.md`, so a future update is a
   clean diff to re-evaluate.
5. Grant it to `angular-developer`, `test-engineer`, `code-reviewer` and `architect` (forms
   ADR only). Do not grant it to `spec-writer` or `strapi-developer`.

### Human decision

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Decision (ADOPT / ADOPT WITH ADJUSTMENTS / REJECT) | |
| Decided by | |
| Date | |
| Notes / conditions | |

---

## EVAL-002 — analogjs/angular-skills (rejected alternative)

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Evaluation date | 2026-11-20 |
| Source URL | https://github.com/analogjs/angular-skills |
| HEAD commit | `18996fd1b2bf663c978065a8d5417393e72ccc6a` (2026-08-06), "Remove skill guidance, leaving deprecation tombstones" |
| License | MIT |
| Status | **Deprecated.** Repo description: "DEPRECATED - use the official Angular skills at https://github.com/angular/skills instead". The README states it is no longer maintained. Not archived. |

### Findings

- All 10 `SKILL.md` files (`angular-component`, `-di`, `-directives`, `-forms`, `-http`,
  `-routing`, `-signals`, `-ssr`, `-testing`, `-tooling`) are about 1 KB tombstones. The
  guidance was removed and only a deprecation notice with a redirect to angular/skills
  remains.
- **Additional risk:** the frontmatter `description` fields still contain the old triggers
  (for example `angular-forms`: "…Signal Forms are experimental but recommended…"). If
  installed, they would activate on form tasks, load no guidance, and carry an outdated
  claim (Signal Forms have been stable since v22.0).

### Verdict: **REJECT**

It is deprecated, contains no guidance, and its own maintainers redirect to angular/skills,
which is evaluated in EVAL-001.

### Human decision

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Decision | |
| Decided by | |
| Date | |
| Notes | |

## Evaluación de `angular-developer`: **ADOPTAR CON AJUSTES**

La dejé registrada en `docs/skills/third-party-evaluation.md`, todavía sin commit. No instalé nada.

- **Commit evaluado**: `97c663a` (2026-11-20). El repo es un espejo que se genera desde `angular/angular` (commit `8b15295`) y se sincroniza varias veces al día. Está activo, no deprecado.

- **Seguridad**: solo contiene Markdown; no hay scripts, hooks ni Unicode oculto. Los únicos dominios externos son `angular.dev`, `api.example.com` y `localhost`. Lo que sí descarga cosas son los `npx` que sugiere (`ng new` con `@latest` y el MCP server de Angular CLI).
- **Riesgo de cadena de suministro**: `npx skills add` instala lo que haya en HEAD, no el commit que evalué. Por eso propongo hacer un diff contra `97c663a` después de instalar.

**Compatibilidad**
- Cumple con Angular 22 (la última estable es la **22.3.0**), standalone, signals, `@if/@for`, Vitest zoneless y sin NgModules.
- Playwright: la skill es neutral. Sugiere un schematic comunitario que no usaremos.
- A11y por teclado: solo la cubre en parte (widgets ARIA). El foco del wizard y los errores accesibles los sigue cubriendo nuestro `review-checklist`.

**Choques con nuestras reglas (todos se resuelven en CLAUDE.md, sin tocar los archivos de la skill)**
- **C1**: `signal-forms.md` dice que **todo** formulario debe ser Signal Forms, y eso decidiría el ADR antes que nosotros. Se resuelve con una precedencia: CLAUDE.md > ADRs aceptados > skills propias > skills de terceros.
- **C2**: hace `ng new` sin fijar versión. Se resuelve fijando la versión del CLI.
- **C3**: propone configurar un MCP server. No se usa, porque nada de herramientas externas.
- **C5**: su convención de nombres es ambigua. La decidimos explícitamente en CLAUDE.md.

**Qué aporta que no tengamos**: la API de Signal Forms al día, con su tabla de errores comunes. Es justo donde un modelo más fácilmente inventa APIs. También aporta testing zoneless con Vitest, `httpResource` para estados de carga y error, y configuración en tiempo de ejecución para servir CO y CL con un mismo build.

**Signal Forms frente a Reactive Forms (para el ADR)**: la skill se contradice. Un archivo dice "v21+ / MUST" y el otro "estable en v22+ / prefer". Lo comprobé en la fuente:

- **A favor de Signal Forms**: encaja con un modelo construido en tiempo de ejecución desde Strapi.
- **En contra**: el tipado queda en `Record<…>`, no admite `null` y hay que probar con un spike qué pasa con números requeridos y fechas vacías.

**analogjs/angular-skills** queda registrada como RECHAZADA. Confirmé lo que me dijiste: está deprecada, el último commit es del 2026-08-06 y sus 10 SKILL.md son lápidas que solo redirigen. # CLAUDE.md

Global context for every agent working in this repository (main session and subagents).
The rules here are binding. If a rule seems wrong, stop and ask the human; do not work around it.

> This file is being built incrementally. The agentic flow sections (agents, checkpoints,
> traceability, session handoff) are added when the flow files are created.

## 1. Precedence of instructions

When two sources of guidance disagree, the higher one wins:

1. **`CLAUDE.md`** (this file)
2. **Accepted ADRs** in `adr/` (status `Accepted`; `Proposed` ADRs are not binding)
3. **Project skills**: skills in `.claude/skills/` written for this project
4. **Third-party skills**: vendored skills listed in `.claude/skills/THIRD_PARTY.md`

A third-party skill never overrides a project decision. If one tells you to do something that a
higher source forbids or has not yet decided, follow the higher source and note the conflict in
your output.

## 2. Language

- Everything in the repository is in **English**: code, identifiers, comments, Markdown docs
  (README, FLOW, specs, ADRs, reviews), commit messages, branch names, PRs, review comments,
  and agent and skill definitions.
- **End-user content is in Spanish**: Strapi seed data (labels, help texts, error messages,
  plans, coverages, terms and conditions), because the users are in Colombia and Chile.

## 3. Security and data

- Never print tokens, secrets or the contents of `.env` files in any output.
- `.env` is git-ignored. Only `.env.example` with fictitious values is committed.
- Only fictitious data anywhere in the repo (people, documents, plates, cards).
- No Strapi token with write permissions may reach the browser.
- Do not use skills, plugins or memory from the user's global `~/.claude`. Everything the flow
  uses is versioned in this repository.

## 4. Toolchain versions (pinned)

| Tool | Version | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| Angular CLI / framework | **22.3.0** (latest stable, verified on npm on 2026-11-20) | Scaffold with `npx @angular/cli@22.3.0 new …`. **Never use `@latest`** or an unpinned `npx @angular/cli`. Pin exact versions in `package.json` (no `^`/`~` on `@angular/*`). |
| Unit tests | Vitest (Angular 22 CLI default) | — |
| E2E tests | `@playwright/test` | Do not use `playwright-ng-schematics` unless a human approves it. |

Upgrading any pinned version requires an ADR or an explicit human approval recorded in the
relevant `tasks.md`.

## 5. Third-party skill overrides

These rules override the vendored `angular-developer` skill (see
`docs/skills/third-party-evaluation.md`, EVAL-001):

- **Forms strategy is not taken from the skill.** `references/signal-forms.md` says Signal Forms
  are mandatory. Ignore that: Signal Forms vs Reactive Forms is decided by an ADR after
  SPIKE-01 (see §7). Until that ADR is accepted, do not write production form code.
- **The Angular CLI MCP server is not used.** Do not configure it (`references/mcp.md`) and do
  not run `npx @angular/cli mcp`.
- **The Angular CLI version is pinned** (§4). The skill's "no version / `@latest`" defaults do
  not apply.
- **Naming follows §6**, not the skill's ambiguous examples.
- **Keyboard accessibility of the wizard** is enforced by the project `review-checklist` skill.
  The skill's ARIA guidance is supplementary.
- Reads of `angular.dev` are allowed as a reference, but any decision based on them must be
  written into a spec or ADR.
- Never edit vendored skill files. Overrides go here.

## 6. Naming conventions

Status: **Proposed** — pending human approval.

The rule is to follow the Angular 22 CLI defaults (no role suffix in file or class names)
and to use **intent-revealing names** so the role stays obvious without a suffix.

### Angular (`frontend/`)

| Artifact | File | Identifier | Example |
|---|---|---|---|
| Component | `kebab-case.ts` + `.html` + `.css` (same base name) | `PascalCase`, no `Component` suffix | `plan-list.ts` → `PlanList` |
| Routed page (wizard step) | `<step>-page.ts` | `…Page` | `quote-form-page.ts` → `QuoteFormPage` |
| Service: HTTP access | `<domain>-api.ts` | `…Api` | `country-content-api.ts` → `CountryContentApi` |
| Service: signal state | `<domain>-store.ts` | `…Store` | `quote-store.ts` → `QuoteStore` |
| Guard / interceptor / resolver (functions) | `<name>-guard.ts`, `-interceptor.ts`, `-resolver.ts` | `camelCase` + role | `wizard-step-guard.ts` → `wizardStepGuard` |
| Pipe | `<name>-pipe.ts` | `…Pipe`; template name `camelCase` | `masked-document-pipe.ts` → `MaskedDocumentPipe` / `maskedDocument` |
| Directive | `<name>.ts` | `PascalCase` | `autofocus-error.ts` → `AutofocusError` |
| Types / models | `<domain>.model.ts` | `PascalCase` interfaces and types, no `I` prefix | `field-config.model.ts` → `FieldConfig` |
| Pure functions | `<domain>.ts` | `camelCase` exported functions | `price-rules.ts` → `calculateFinalPrice()` |
| Validators | `<domain>-validators.ts` | `camelCase` factories | `field-validators.ts` → `legalAge()` |
| Unit tests | `<same-base-name>.spec.ts` next to the file | `describe('<US-AC id> …')` | `price-rules.spec.ts` |
| E2E tests | `frontend/e2e/<us-ids>-<slug>.spec.ts` | `test('<US-AC id> …')` | `us-01-03-full-flow-co.spec.ts` |
| Component selector prefix | — | `app-` | `app-plan-card` |
| Constants and injection tokens | in the file that owns them | `UPPER_SNAKE_CASE` | `STRAPI_BASE_URL` |

Folders: `src/app/core/` (singletons, API clients, interceptors), `src/app/features/<feature>/`
(wizard steps), `src/app/shared/` (reusable presentational UI, pipes, pure functions).

### Strapi (`backend/`)

- Content-type API IDs: singular `kebab-case` (`form-field`, `plan`, `country`, `terms`).
- Components: `category.kebab-name` (`form.select-option`, `plan.coverage`).
- Attribute names: `camelCase` (`isRecommended`, `sortOrder`, `errorMessage`).
- Custom code files: `kebab-case.ts`.

### Repository artifacts

- Specs: `specs/US-01/{story,spec,tasks}.md`
- ADRs: `adr/NNNN-kebab-title.md` (4-digit, sequential)
- Reviews: `reviews/US-01-review-R1.md`
- Branches: `feat/us-01-short-slug`, `fix/us-01-…`, `chore/…`, `docs/…`

## 7. Pending decisions

| ID | Decision | How it will be resolved | Blocks |
|---|---|---|---|
| SPIKE-01 | **Signal Forms vs Reactive Forms** for the Strapi-driven step 1 form | Throwaway spike (30–60 min) on a branch that is not merged: a minimal form built from a Strapi-like JSON with a **required number**, an **empty date**, a **select**, and a **legal-age validation**. It also checks how typing degrades with a runtime model. The findings feed an ADR (alternatives, consequences); a human accepts it. | Production form code for US-01 |

---
name: sdd-spec
description: Turns a functional user story into a verifiable spec (this project's Spec-Driven Development variant). Use when writing or revising specs/US-XX/spec.md or specs/US-XX/tasks.md, when detecting gaps in a user story, or when assigning BR/AC/Q/T identifiers.
---

# SDD spec procedure

The spec is the **source of truth**: code and tests are derived from it, never the other way
around. If the implementation needs something that the spec does not say, the spec changes
first, and the change needs human approval (HC1).

## Inputs and outputs

- **Input:** `specs/US-XX/story.md`, the user story copied verbatim by a human. Never edit it.
- **Outputs:**
  - `specs/US-XX/spec.md`, built from [templates/spec.md](templates/spec.md)
  - `specs/US-XX/tasks.md`, built from [templates/tasks.md](templates/tasks.md)
- **Read before writing:** `CLAUDE.md`, the accepted ADRs in `adr/`, and the specs of the
  other stories (to keep shared concepts consistent).

## Identifiers (never renumber; retire with ~~strikethrough~~ + reason)

| Kind | Format | Example |
|---|---|---|
| Business rule | `US-XX-BR-NN` | `US-01-BR-03` |
| Acceptance criterion | `US-XX-AC-NN` | `US-01-AC-02` |
| Gap / open question | `US-XX-Q-NN` | `US-01-Q-04` |
| Task | `US-XX-T-NN` | `US-01-T-07` |

- Each Gherkin scenario in the story becomes one AC and keeps its original title.
- ACs that **you** derive (from a business rule, a gap answer or a non-functional requirement)
  are marked `(derived from US-XX-BR-NN / Q-NN)`. Every business rule must be covered by at
  least one AC; otherwise it is not verifiable.

## Procedure

1. Read the story and copy every business rule as written. Then add a **refined** version that
   is precise and testable (numbers, boundaries, units, timezone).
2. Run the gap-detection checklist below. Each hit becomes a `Q` entry with:
   the problem, why it matters, **a proposed default**, and an empty *Human answer* field.
3. Write the ACs in Gherkin. Use concrete fictitious example values (scenario outlines with
   tables for boundaries). One behaviour per scenario.
4. Fill in the remaining template sections: content contract (what Strapi must provide),
   UI states, non-functional requirements, test mapping, and ADRs referenced or needed.
5. If a decision is architectural (it affects more than one story, is hard to reverse, or
   chooses between technologies or patterns), do **not** decide it in the spec. List it under
   *ADRs needed* for the architect.
6. Set the status to `Draft — awaiting HC1`. Write `tasks.md` (tasks are small: ≤ ~1 h of agent
   work, each tied to ACs).
7. Never mark a spec `Approved`; only the human does that in the *Review log*.

## Gap-detection checklist

Ask each question of the story. A "we don't know" answer is a gap.

- **Ambiguous words:** "simple", "clear", "suited", "usually", "partially", "etc." What exactly?
- **Boundaries:** exact limits and whether they are inclusive (age exactly 18 today? year = next
  year? 20 years counted from what date?). Which timezone defines "today"?
- **Data shape:** for each field, the type, format, min/max length, allowed characters and
  normalisation (dots/dashes in RUT, plate format, upper case).
- **Country context:** how does the app know the country (URL, selector, domain)? What happens
  with an unknown or unsupported country? Can the user switch country mid-flow?
- **Content ownership:** which texts come from Strapi and which are in code (buttons, step
  titles, generic errors)? What if Strapi content is missing or malformed?
- **States:** loading, empty, error (Strapi down, timeout), partial content, retry.
- **Persistence:** what survives a reload or back navigation? When is the stored data cleared
  (after payment? on country switch)? Is anything sensitive persisted?
- **Navigation:** can the user deep-link to step 2 or 3 without completing earlier steps? What
  does browser back do?
- **Concurrency and idempotency:** double clicks, double submits, retries.
- **Draft vs published, active vs inactive:** which combinations are visible?
- **Formatting:** currency, decimals, thousand separators, date format per country.
- **Security and privacy:** masking rules (which characters are shown), what is logged, what
  reaches the browser.
- **Accessibility:** keyboard path, focus on step change and on errors, labels, error announcements.
- **Responsive:** mobile layout of complex parts (plan comparison, summary).
- **Configuration change:** what happens if content changes while a user is mid-flow?
- **Verifiability:** can each criterion be checked by an automated test? If not, why not, and how
  will it be checked manually?

## Quality bar for HC1 (self-check before handing over)

- [ ] Every business rule is refined and covered by ≥ 1 AC.
- [ ] Every AC is observable and testable, with concrete example values.
- [ ] Every gap has a proposed default; nothing is silently assumed.
- [ ] Out-of-scope items are explicit.
- [ ] No contradiction with accepted ADRs; needed ADRs are listed.
- [ ] Each AC has a planned test level (unit / component / e2e / manual).
- [ ] `tasks.md` exists, and every task references ACs.

---
name: sdd-spec
description: Turns a functional user story into a verifiable spec (this project's Spec-Driven Development variant). Use when writing or revising specs/US-XX/spec.md or specs/US-XX/tasks.md, when detecting gaps in a user story, or when assigning BR/AC/Q/T identifiers.
---

# SDD spec procedure

The spec is the **source of truth**: code and tests are derived from it, never the other way
around. If the implementation needs something that the spec does not say, the spec changes
first, and the change needs human approval (HC1).

## Inputs and outputs

- **Input:** `specs/US-XX/story.md`, the user story copied verbatim by a human. Never edit it.
- **Outputs:**
  - `specs/US-XX/spec.md`, built from [templates/spec.md](templates/spec.md)
  - `specs/US-XX/tasks.md`, built from [templates/tasks.md](templates/tasks.md)
- **Read before writing:** `CLAUDE.md`, the accepted ADRs in `adr/`, and the specs of the
  other stories (to keep shared concepts consistent).

## Identifiers (never renumber; retire with ~~strikethrough~~ + reason)

| Kind | Format | Example |
|---|---|---|
| Business rule | `US-XX-BR-NN` | `US-01-BR-03` |
| Acceptance criterion | `US-XX-AC-NN` | `US-01-AC-02` |
| Gap / open question | `US-XX-Q-NN` | `US-01-Q-04` |
| Task | `US-XX-T-NN` | `US-01-T-07` |

- Each Gherkin scenario in the story becomes one AC and keeps its original title.
- ACs that **you** derive (from a business rule, a gap answer or a non-functional requirement)
  are marked `(derived from US-XX-BR-NN / Q-NN)`. Every business rule must be covered by at
  least one AC; otherwise it is not verifiable.

## Procedure

1. Read the story and copy every business rule as written. Then add a **refined** version that
   is precise and testable (numbers, boundaries, units, timezone).
2. Run the gap-detection checklist below. Each hit becomes a `Q` entry with:
   the problem, why it matters, **a proposed default**, and an empty *Human answer* field.
3. Write the ACs in Gherkin. Use concrete fictitious example values (scenario outlines with
   tables for boundaries). One behaviour per scenario.
4. Fill in the remaining template sections: content contract (what Strapi must provide),
   UI states, non-functional requirements, test mapping, and ADRs referenced or needed.
5. If a decision is architectural (it affects more than one story, is hard to reverse, or
   chooses between technologies or patterns), do **not** decide it in the spec. List it under
   *ADRs needed* for the architect.
6. Set the status to `Draft — awaiting HC1`. Write `tasks.md` (tasks are small: ≤ ~1 h of agent
   work, each tied to ACs).
7. Never mark a spec `Approved`; only the human does that in the *Review log*.

## Gap-detection checklist

Ask each question of the story. A "we don't know" answer is a gap.

- **Ambiguous words:** "simple", "clear", "suited", "usually", "partially", "etc." What exactly?
- **Boundaries:** exact limits and whether they are inclusive (age exactly 18 today? year = next
  year? 20 years counted from what date?). Which timezone defines "today"?
- **Data shape:** for each field, the type, format, min/max length, allowed characters and
  normalisation (dots/dashes in RUT, plate format, upper case).
- **Country context:** how does the app know the country (URL, selector, domain)? What happens
  with an unknown or unsupported country? Can the user switch country mid-flow?
- **Content ownership:** which texts come from Strapi and which are in code (buttons, step
  titles, generic errors)? What if Strapi content is missing or malformed?
- **States:** loading, empty, error (Strapi down, timeout), partial content, retry.
- **Persistence:** what survives a reload or back navigation? When is the stored data cleared
  (after payment? on country switch)? Is anything sensitive persisted?
- **Navigation:** can the user deep-link to step 2 or 3 without completing earlier steps? What
  does browser back do?
- **Concurrency and idempotency:** double clicks, double submits, retries.
- **Draft vs published, active vs inactive:** which combinations are visible?
- **Formatting:** currency, decimals, thousand separators, date format per country.
- **Security and privacy:** masking rules (which characters are shown), what is logged, what
  reaches the browser.
- **Accessibility:** keyboard path, focus on step change and on errors, labels, error announcements.
- **Responsive:** mobile layout of complex parts (plan comparison, summary).
- **Configuration change:** what happens if content changes while a user is mid-flow?
- **Verifiability:** can each criterion be checked by an automated test? If not, why not, and how
  will it be checked manually?

## Quality bar for HC1 (self-check before handing over)

- [ ] Every business rule is refined and covered by ≥ 1 AC.
- [ ] Every AC is observable and testable, with concrete example values.
- [ ] Every gap has a proposed default; nothing is silently assumed.
- [ ] Out-of-scope items are explicit.
- [ ] No contradiction with accepted ADRs; needed ADRs are listed.
- [ ] Each AC has a planned test level (unit / component / e2e / manual).
- [ ] `tasks.md` exists, and every task references ACs.

---
name: adr-madr
description: Writes Architecture Decision Records in MADR 4 format for this project. Use when a spec lists "ADRs needed", when choosing between technologies or patterns, or when superseding an existing ADR in adr/.
---

# ADRs (MADR 4)

## When a decision deserves an ADR

Write one if **any** of these is true:

- It affects more than one user story or more than one layer (Angular + Strapi).
- It is expensive to reverse (data model, content strategy, state management, security model).
- There were at least two reasonable options, and someone could later ask "why this one?".
- It overrides guidance from a third-party skill or a framework default.

Do **not** write an ADR for local implementation details that the spec or code review covers.

## Rules

- File: `adr/NNNN-kebab-title.md`, 4-digit sequential number. Never reuse a number. Use the
  template in [templates/adr.md](templates/adr.md).
- **At least two real alternatives**, each with honest pros and cons. A strawman option
  ("do nothing" with no merit) does not count as an alternative.
- Decision drivers must trace back to requirements: the assessment PDF, a spec `BR`/`AC`, or
  `CLAUDE.md`.
- Consequences include the **bad** ones and how they are mitigated.
- *Confirmation* says how compliance is checked: a test, a review checklist item, a script.
- Facts about libraries (versions, API stability) must be verified against the official source
  or the installed package, with a link or version. Never state them from memory.
- If a spike informed the decision, link its findings (the branch is not merged; summarise the
  results in the ADR).

## Lifecycle (the status changes only by these rules)

| Status | Who sets it | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `Proposed` | architect subagent | Ready for HC2. Not binding. |
| `Accepted` | **human only** | Binding (precedence level 2 in `CLAUDE.md`). Record `Decided by` and date. |
| `Rejected` | **human only** | Kept in the repo, with the reason. |
| `Superseded by ADR-NNNN` | architect, after the new ADR is accepted | Old file kept, with a link to the replacement. |

Accepted ADRs are never rewritten. A change of mind means a new ADR that supersedes the old one.

## Index

Keep `adr/README.md` updated: number, title, status, date, related stories.

---
name: review-checklist
description: Code review procedure, checklist, severities and report format for this project. Use when reviewing a story branch or PR (code-reviewer subagent), when verifying fixes for review findings, or when a developer self-checks before requesting review.
---

# Code review checklist

The reviewer **finds** problems and **never fixes them**. Each finding is concrete (file:line),
reproducible, and tied to a rule (spec AC/BR, ADR, `CLAUDE.md`, or a checklist item below).
Write the report with [templates/review.md](templates/review.md) at
`reviews/US-XX-review-RN.md` (N = review round, starting at 1).

## Procedure

1. Read `specs/US-XX/spec.md`, the accepted ADRs it references, and `tasks.md`.
2. Get the diff: `git diff main...HEAD` (plus `git log main..HEAD` for commit traceability).
3. Run the automated checks yourself and paste a summary of the results (lint, typecheck, unit,
   e2e, build). **Do not trust a developer's claim that the tests pass.**
4. Walk through **every AC**: find the code that implements it and the test that proves it. Run
   `scripts/trace.sh US-XX`.
5. Go through the checklist. Record every finding with a severity.
6. Verdict: `APPROVED` (no open blocker/major findings) or `CHANGES REQUESTED`.

In round N+1, verify each earlier finding against its fix commit, set its status, and add any
new findings.

## Severities

| Severity | Meaning | Blocks merge? |
|---|---|---|
| **blocker** | Violates security rules, breaks an AC, loses user data, or does not build | Yes |
| **major** | AC partially met, missing state handling, a11y failure, missing test for an AC, ADR violation | Yes |
| **minor** | Maintainability, weak typing, unclear naming, a small UX inconsistency | No (fix or justify) |
| **nit** | Style or preference | No |

A `minor`/`nit` may be closed as `won't fix` with a justification. A `blocker`/`major` may not.

## Checklist

### Spec conformance and traceability
- [ ] Every AC is implemented, and nothing was implemented that the spec does not ask for (scope creep).
- [ ] Every AC has at least one test named with its ID, and the test asserts behaviour, not
      implementation details.
- [ ] Commits reference US/AC/ADR IDs, and fix commits reference finding IDs.

### Security
- [ ] No Strapi token with write permissions in frontend code, environment files, the bundle or
      network calls.
- [ ] The Strapi public role only has the `find`/`findOne` permissions justified in the ADR.
- [ ] No secrets or `.env` contents committed; `.env.example` holds fictitious values only.
- [ ] Rich text from Strapi (terms, help texts) is rendered safely: no `bypassSecurityTrust*`, and
      `[innerHTML]` only with Angular sanitisation.
- [ ] Sensitive data (document numbers) is masked as the spec says and is not logged to the console.
- [ ] Only fictitious data in seeds, fixtures and tests.

### Multi-country and configurability
- [ ] No hard-coded country-specific values in code (labels, field lists, currency, document
      types, plans, terms). They come from Strapi, per the multi-country ADR.
- [ ] Adding or reordering a field or plan in Strapi requires no code change. Verify against
      the AC scenario.
- [ ] Currency and number formatting comes from the country's configuration or locale (CLP and
      COP have no decimals in display).
- [ ] The same build serves both countries (no per-country build flags).

### Angular (see CLAUDE.md overrides; the vendored angular-developer skill is reference only)
- [ ] Standalone components only; no NgModules authored; `@if/@for/@switch` with `track`.
- [ ] State in signals (`signal`, `computed`, `linkedSignal`, `resource`/`httpResource`).
      `effect` is used only for real side effects.
- [ ] `inject()` instead of constructor injection; `input()`/`output()`/`model()` APIs.
- [ ] No `any`. Strapi responses are typed and validated at the boundary (malformed content
      does not crash the app).
- [ ] Loading, empty and error states exist for every remote call, with a retry where the spec
      asks for one.
- [ ] Naming follows `CLAUDE.md` §6.
- [ ] Forms follow the accepted forms ADR (not the third-party skill's default).

### Strapi
- [ ] Content types follow the `strapi-content-modeling` skill and the multi-country ADR.
- [ ] The seed is idempotent and creates **published** content for both CO and CL.
- [ ] Public permissions are set in code (bootstrap), not by hand in the admin panel.

### Accessibility (keyboard-only completion is a hard requirement)
- [ ] The whole wizard can be completed with Tab / Shift+Tab / Enter / Space / arrow keys. Check it.
- [ ] Every field has a programmatic label. Help and error texts are linked via `aria-describedby`;
      invalid fields have `aria-invalid`.
- [ ] On a failed submit, focus moves to the first invalid field (or an error summary).
- [ ] On a step change, focus moves to the step heading, and the step change is announced.
- [ ] Plan selection uses a native radio group or an equivalent ARIA pattern. The recommended
      badge is not conveyed by colour alone.
- [ ] Visible focus indicator; contrast ≥ 4.5:1 for text.
- [ ] Disabled pay button: its state is perceivable, and the reason (terms not accepted) is explained.

### Responsive
- [ ] Usable at 360 px wide and on desktop. No horizontal scroll; touch targets ≥ 44 px.

### Tests
- [ ] Unit tests cover the logic (validators, price rule, masking, config mapping), including boundaries.
- [ ] E2E tests use role or label locators (`getByRole`, `getByLabel`), have no fixed sleeps, and
      run against the seeded stack.
- [ ] Tests fail when the behaviour breaks: mentally mutate the code. Would the test catch it?

### Language
- [ ] Code, comments and docs in English; end-user content (seed) in Spanish.

# ADRs (MADR 4)

## When a decision deserves an ADR

Write one if **any** of these is true:

- It affects more than one user story or more than one layer (Angular + Strapi).

  template in [templates/adr.md](templates/adr.md).

  ("do nothing" with no merit) does not count as an alternative.
- Decision drivers must trace back to requirements: the assessment PDF, a spec `BR`/`AC`, or

- If a spike informed the decision, link its findings (the branch is not merged; summarise the

  **2. Restricting Write/Edit paths for a subagent**

  ```yaml
  ---
  name: spec-writer
  description: Writes specs under specs/ only
  tools: Read, Glob, Grep, Write, Edit, Bash
  hooks:
    PreToolUse:
      - matcher: "Write|Edit"
        hooks:
          - type: command

  ---
  ```

  **3. PreToolUse stdin JSON**
  Source: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks.md
  Common fields: `session_id`, `prompt_id`, `transcript_path`, `cwd`, `scratchpad_dir`, `permission_mode`, `effort` (object with `level`), `hook_event_name`.

  **4. settings.json PreToolUse schema and blocking**
  Source: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks.md
  ```json
  {
    "hooks": {
      "PreToolUse": [
        {
          "matcher": "Read|Edit|Write",
          "hooks": [
            { "type": "command",
              "command": "\"$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR\"/.claude/hooks/guard.sh" }

    }
  }
  ```
  - Matcher rules: `"*"`, empty, or omitted matches all. Letters, digits, `_`, `-`, spaces, `,`, and `|` mean exact names or lists (`Edit|Write`, `Edit, Write`). Any other character makes it a JavaScript regex, unanchored (`^Edit$` for whole-string). Example from docs: `mcp__memory__.*`.

  Source: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permissions.md
  - Rule form: `Read(<gitignore-style path>)`. `Read(./.env)` matches the .env in the current directory. Bare `.env` or `**/.env` matches at any depth under the current directory, and does not match parent directories. `//**/.env` matches anywhere on the filesystem.

It carves the paths it matches out of the `path` or `./path` rules listed before it." Their example: `Read(*.env)` followed by `Read(!sample.env)`. Analogous config (inferred from that example, not separately documented for `.env.*`):
  ```json

  ```

  Source: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents.md
