# US-02 – Plan list

## Story

As a person getting a quote, I want to see the plans available for my country with their price and coverages, so that I can choose the one that best fits my needs.

## Context

Plans, coverages, benefits and prices change by country and are managed by the business team from Strapi. The business team wants to highlight one plan as “recommended” and control the order in which plans appear.

## Business rules

- Each plan is configured in Strapi with: name, short description, base price, currency, coverages, benefits, order, recommended flag, active status and country.
- Only published and active plans for the country are shown.
- The price is shown in the country’s currency and format (Colombian pesos or Chilean pesos).
- The final price may be adjusted by a simulated rule based on the step 1 data. The rule is documented.
- Only one plan can be selected.

## Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Scenario: Plans for the country
  Given I completed the step 1 form
  When I reach the plans step
  Then I see only the active and published plans for my country, in the configured order

Scenario: Recommended plan
  Given a plan is marked as recommended in Strapi
  When I view the plan list
  Then that plan is visually distinguished from the others

Scenario: Plan selection
  Given I am on the plan list
  When I select a plan
  Then it is marked as chosen
  And I can move on to the summary

Scenario: No plans available
  Given there are no active plans for my country
  When I reach the plans step
  Then I see a message explaining that no plans are available
```

# US-03 – Summary and payment

## Story

As a person who chose a plan, I want to review a summary of my quote and pay, so that I become insured.

## Context

Before paying, the person must confirm their data and accept the terms and conditions, whose text varies by country and is managed by the business team from Strapi. Payment is simulated for this test.

## Business rules

- The summary shows the policyholder’s data, the vehicle’s data and the chosen plan with its final price.
- The document number is shown partially masked.
- From the summary the person can go back to edit their data or change the plan.
- The pay button is enabled only after accepting the terms and conditions.
- The payment cannot be submitted twice.
- On successful payment, a confirmation with a simulated quote number is shown.

## Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Scenario: Complete summary
  Given I chose a plan
  When I reach the summary
  Then I see my data, my vehicle’s data and the chosen plan with its final price

Scenario: Terms by country
  Given I am on the summary
  When I view the terms and conditions
  Then the text matches the one configured in Strapi for my country
  And the pay button is disabled until I accept them

Scenario: Successful payment
  Given I accepted the terms
  When I click pay
  Then the button is locked while the payment is processed
  And I see the confirmation with the quote number

Scenario: Rejected payment
  Given the simulated payment fails
  When I click pay
  Then I see a clear error message
  And I can try again without losing my information
```

# US-01 – Policyholder and vehicle data form

## Story

As a person interested in insuring my car, I want to enter my data and my vehicle’s data in a simple form, so that I receive insurance options suited to my country and my vehicle.

## Context

Fields change by country. In Colombia the identity document is usually the citizenship ID (cédula de ciudadanía) or foreigner ID (cédula de extranjería), and the vehicle is identified by its license plate (placa). In Chile the document is the RUT and the vehicle is identified by its license plate (patente). The business team wants to add, remove or reorder fields from Strapi without asking development for changes.

## Business rules

- Each field is configured in Strapi with: label, type (text, number, select, date, checkbox), required flag, validations, help text, error message, order and country.
- Select fields (for example, make or city) get their options from Strapi.
- The vehicle year cannot be later than next year or more than 20 years old.
- The policyholder must be of legal age.

## Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Scenario: Form configured by country
  Given fields are configured in Strapi for Colombia and for Chile
  When I open the application in the context of a country
  Then I see only the fields configured for that country, in the defined order

Scenario: Field validation
  Given I am filling out the form
  When a field does not meet its configured validation
  Then I see the configured error message next to the field
  And I cannot move to the next step

Scenario: Configuration change without deployment
  Given the business team adds a new published field in Strapi
  When I reload the application
  Then the new field appears without code changes

Scenario: Keep data when going back
  Given I moved on to step 2
  When I go back to step 1
  Then my data is still filled in
```

# US-02 – Plan list

## Story

As a person getting a quote, I want to see the plans available for my country with their price and coverages, so that I can choose the one that best fits my needs.

## Context

Plans, coverages, benefits and prices change by country and are managed by the business team from Strapi. The business team wants to highlight one plan as “recommended” and control the order in which plans appear.

## Business rules

- Each plan is configured in Strapi with: name, short description, base price, currency, coverages, benefits, order, recommended flag, active status and country.
- Only published and active plans for the country are shown.
- The price is shown in the country’s currency and format (Colombian pesos or Chilean pesos).
- The final price may be adjusted by a simulated rule based on the step 1 data. The rule is documented.
- Only one plan can be selected.

## Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Scenario: Plans for the country
  Given I completed the step 1 form
  When I reach the plans step
  Then I see only the active and published plans for my country, in the configured order

  When I view the plan list
  Then that plan is visually distinguished from the others

Scenario: Plan selection
  Given I am on the plan list
  When I select a plan
  Then it is marked as chosen
  And I can move on to the summary

Scenario: No plans available
  Given there are no active plans for my country
  When I reach the plans step
  Then I see a message explaining that no plans are available
```

# US-03 – Summary and payment

## Story

As a person who chose a plan, I want to review a summary of my quote and pay, so that I become insured.

## Context

Before paying, the person must confirm their data and accept the terms and conditions, whose text varies by country and is managed by the business team from Strapi. Payment is simulated for this test.

## Business rules

- The summary shows the policyholder’s data, the vehicle’s data and the chosen plan with its final price.
- The document number is shown partially masked.
- From the summary the person can go back to edit their data or change the plan.
- The pay button is enabled only after accepting the terms and conditions.
- The payment cannot be submitted twice.
- On successful payment, a confirmation with a simulated quote number is shown.

## Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Scenario: Complete summary
  Given I chose a plan
  When I reach the summary
  Then I see my data, my vehicle’s data and the chosen plan with its final price

Scenario: Successful payment

  And I see the confirmation with the quote number

Scenario: Rejected payment
  Given the simulated payment fails
  When I click pay
  Then I see a clear error message
  And I can try again without losing my information
```

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Check that specs/US-NN/story.md files are verbatim transcriptions of the assessment PDF.

Usage (run with `python3 -I` so nothing is imported from the current directory):
    python3 -I scripts/check-story-fidelity.py <assessment.pdf> specs/US-01/story.md [...]

How it works (deterministic, no AI):
  1. `pdftotext -enc UTF-8` extracts the PDF text (requires poppler).
  2. Page furniture is removed (the "English" header and the "Page N of 9" footers).
  3. From each story, the provenance comment, the code fences and the Markdown markers are removed.
  4. Both texts are tokenised into words and punctuation (curly quotes kept). The story's tokens
     must appear as one contiguous run in the PDF tokens. Whitespace and line wraps are ignored
     on purpose: joining wrapped lines is the only allowed change.

Exits 1 if any story differs from the PDF or cannot be located in it.
"""
import re
import subprocess
import sys

TOKEN = re.compile(r"[\w’‘“”()-]+|[.,:;!?]")


def pdf_tokens(pdf_path: str) -> list[str]:
    text = subprocess.run(
        ["pdftotext", "-enc", "UTF-8", pdf_path, "-"],
        check=True, capture_output=True, text=True,
    ).stdout
    text = re.sub(r"Page \d+ of \d+", " ", text)
    text = re.sub(r"\bEnglish\b", " ", text)
    return TOKEN.findall(text)


def story_tokens(path: str) -> list[str]:
    with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        text = fh.read()
    text = re.sub(r"<!--.*?-->", " ", text, flags=re.S)
    text = re.sub(r"```\w*", " ", text)
    text = re.sub(r"(?m)^#+ ", " ", text)
    text = re.sub(r"(?m)^- ", " ", text)
    return TOKEN.findall(text)


def main() -> int:
    if len(sys.argv) < 3:
        print(__doc__, file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    source = pdf_tokens(sys.argv[1])
    failed = False
    for story in sys.argv[2:]:
        tokens = story_tokens(story)
        head = tokens[:6]
        starts = [i for i in range(len(source)) if source[i:i + len(head)] == head]
        if not starts:
            print(f"FAIL {story}: start not found in PDF ({' '.join(head)} …)")
            failed = True
            continue
        best = None
        for start in starts:
            segment = source[start:start + len(tokens)]
            diffs = [(k, a, b) for k, (a, b) in enumerate(zip(tokens, segment)) if a != b]
            if len(segment) < len(tokens):
                diffs.append((len(segment), "<story continues>", "<PDF ended>"))
            if best is None or len(diffs) < len(best):
                best = diffs
        if best:
            failed = True
            print(f"FAIL {story}: {len(best)} difference(s) in {len(tokens)} tokens")
            for k, ours, theirs in best[:10]:
                print(f"     token {k}: story={ours!r} pdf={theirs!r}")
        else:
            print(f"OK   {story}: {len(tokens)} tokens identical to the PDF")
    return 1 if failed else 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

# AGENTS.md

Catalogue of the AI agents and skills used in this repository.

- **Binding conventions** for every agent are in [CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md). If you use a tool
  other than Claude Code that reads `AGENTS.md`, read `CLAUDE.md` first: it is the single source
  of rules, and this file does not repeat them.
- **The flow** (order, checkpoints, approval criteria) is in [FLOW.md](FLOW.md).

## Subagents (`.claude/agents/`)

Every subagent has `Agent` disallowed (no nested delegation) and a `PreToolUse` hook that
enforces its write scope (`.claude/hooks/enforce-write-scope.mjs`).

| Agent | Model | Flow step | Inputs | Outputs | Allowed tools | Write scope (enforced) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [spec-writer](.claude/agents/spec-writer.md) | Opus 5.5 | 1 Spec | `story.md`, accepted ADRs, `CLAUDE.md` | `spec.md`, `tasks.md` | Read, Grep, Glob, Write, Edit, Skill | `specs/US-NN/spec.md`, `specs/US-NN/tasks.md` |
| [architect](.claude/agents/architect.md) | Opus 5.5 | 2 ADRs, spike write-ups | approved spec (*ADRs needed*), spike results | `adr/NNNN-*.md` (Proposed), `docs/spikes/*` | Read, Grep, Glob, Write, Edit, Bash (read-only use), WebFetch, Skill | `adr/**`, `docs/spikes/**`, `tasks.md` |
| [test-engineer](.claude/agents/test-engineer.md) | Sonnet 5.5 | 3 Tests first | approved spec, accepted ADRs | unit, component and e2e tests (red) | Read, Grep, Glob, Write, Edit, Bash, Skill | `**/*.spec.ts`, `**/*.test.ts`, `frontend/e2e/**`, `frontend/src/testing/**`, `backend/tests/**`, `tasks.md` |
| [strapi-developer](.claude/agents/strapi-developer.md) | Sonnet 5.5 | 4 Implementation, 7 Fixes | approved spec, ADRs, tests | content types, seed, permissions | Read, Grep, Glob, Write, Edit, Bash, Skill | `backend/**` except tests, `docker-compose.yml`, `.env.example`, `tasks.md` |
| [frontend-developer](.claude/agents/frontend-developer.md) | Sonnet 5.5 | 4 Implementation, 7 Fixes, spikes | approved spec, ADRs, red tests | Angular code | Read, Grep, Glob, Write, Edit, Bash, Skill | `frontend/**` except tests, `spikes/**`, `docker-compose.yml`, `.env.example`, `tasks.md` |

checks their diffs, and talks to the human. It does not do the agents' work on stories.

Las tres historias están transcritas en la rama `docs/h0-intake-us-01-03`. Todavía no hice commit.

**Qué hice**
- Confirmé tu merge del PR #1 y actualicé `main`.
- Transcribí `specs/US-01/story.md`, `US-02/story.md` y `US-03/story.md`. Cada una lleva una cabecera de procedencia, separada del texto: el PDF de origen con su SHA-256 (`4d7ea38e…`), las páginas y una nota de que las transcribí yo por decisión tuya.
- Los únicos cambios de forma son las líneas de Gherkin que el PDF partía por el ancho de página, que volví a unir, y el escenario *Rejected payment*, que estaba repartido entre las páginas 8 y 9.

**Verificación de fidelidad**
- Comparé cada historia palabra por palabra con el texto que extrae `pdftotext` del PDF: **918 tokens, 0 diferencias**, incluidas comillas tipográficas y puntuación.
- La verificación quedó versionada como `scripts/check-story-fidelity.py`. La probé también con una copia alterada en una palabra y una coma: la detecta y sale con código 1.
- Mi primera versión del script daba cientos de diferencias falsas porque no quitaba la cabecera "English" de cada página. La corregí antes de dar el resultado por bueno.

**Registro de tu decisión**
- FLOW.md ahora dice que H0 es "sin IA por defecto" y que US-01..03 son una excepción decidida por ti. El riesgo de que el agente parafrasee lo cubre la verificación mecánica.
- `specs/README.md` y `AGENTS.md` están actualizados.
- El escaneo de secretos sale limpio.

- "The same application and the same build serve Colombia and Chile."
- "Changing a form field or a plan in Strapi must be reflected in the app without changing code."
- "Price calculation may be simulated: a real rating engine is not expected."
- "Use fictitious data only."
- "Use a front-end strategy to persist the data; a database is not required."

- Environment: "The whole project starts with a single command (for example docker compose up), with seed data for both countries"
- Accessibility: "The wizard can be completed using only the keyboard, and fields have accessible labels"
- Responsive: "Works on mobile and desktop"

You are the **spec-writer** of this project's agentic flow (see `FLOW.md`, step 1).

## Responsibility

Produce a spec that a human can approve at HC1 and that the other agents can derive tests and code
from without guessing. You make gaps visible; you do not resolve them silently.

## Inputs

- `specs/US-XX/story.md`: the user story, verbatim. **Read-only; never edit it.**
- `CLAUDE.md`, the accepted ADRs in `adr/`, and the other stories' specs (for consistency).
- On a revision: the human's feedback in the spec's *Review log* and the answers in the *Gaps*
  table.

## Outputs

- `specs/US-XX/spec.md`, following the `sdd-spec` skill and its template.
- `specs/US-XX/tasks.md`, following the template (status `1 Spec`, next action `HC1`).

Write access is enforced by a hook: you can only write those two files.

---
name: sdd-spec
description: Turns a functional user story into a verifiable spec (this project's Spec-Driven Development variant). Use when writing or revising specs/US-XX/spec.md or specs/US-XX/tasks.md, when detecting gaps in a user story, or when assigning BR/AC/Q/T identifiers.
---

# SDD spec procedure

The spec is the **source of truth**: code and tests are derived from it, never the other way
around. If the implementation needs something that the spec does not say, the spec changes
first, and the change needs human approval (HC1).

## Inputs and outputs

- **Input:** `specs/US-XX/story.md`, the user story copied verbatim by a human. Never edit it.
- **Outputs:**
  - `specs/US-XX/spec.md`, built from [templates/spec.md](templates/spec.md)
  - `specs/US-XX/tasks.md`, built from [templates/tasks.md](templates/tasks.md)
- **Read before writing:** `CLAUDE.md`, the accepted ADRs in `adr/`, and the specs of the
  other stories (to keep shared concepts consistent).

## Identifiers (never renumber; retire with ~~strikethrough~~ + reason)

| Kind | Format | Example |
|---|---|---|
| Business rule | `US-XX-BR-NN` | `US-01-BR-03` |
| Acceptance criterion | `US-XX-AC-NN` | `US-01-AC-02` |
| Gap / open question | `US-XX-Q-NN` | `US-01-Q-04` |
| Task | `US-XX-T-NN` | `US-01-T-07` |

- Each Gherkin scenario in the story becomes one AC and keeps its original title.
- ACs that **you** derive (from a business rule, a gap answer or a non-functional requirement)
  are marked `(derived from US-XX-BR-NN / Q-NN)`. Every business rule must be covered by at
  least one AC; otherwise it is not verifiable.

## Procedure

1. Read the story and copy every business rule as written. Then add a **refined** version that
   is precise and testable (numbers, boundaries, units, timezone).
2. Run the gap-detection checklist below. Each hit becomes a `Q` entry with:
   the problem, why it matters, **a proposed default**, and an empty *Human answer* field.
3. Write the ACs in Gherkin. Use concrete fictitious example values (scenario outlines with
   tables for boundaries). One behaviour per scenario.
4. Fill in the remaining template sections: content contract (what Strapi must provide),
   UI states, non-functional requirements, test mapping, and ADRs referenced or needed.
5. If a decision is architectural (it affects more than one story, is hard to reverse, or
   chooses between technologies or patterns), do **not** decide it in the spec. List it under
   *ADRs needed* for the architect.
6. Set the status to `Draft — awaiting HC1`. Write `tasks.md` (tasks are small: ≤ ~1 h of agent
   work, each tied to ACs).
7. Never mark a spec `Approved`; only the human does that in the *Review log*.

## Gap-detection checklist

Ask each question of the story. A "we don't know" answer is a gap.

- **Ambiguous words:** "simple", "clear", "suited", "usually", "partially", "etc." What exactly?
- **Boundaries:** exact limits and whether they are inclusive (age exactly 18 today? year = next
  year? 20 years counted from what date?). Which timezone defines "today"?
- **Data shape:** for each field, the type, format, min/max length, allowed characters and
  normalisation (dots/dashes in RUT, plate format, upper case).
- **Country context:** how does the app know the country (URL, selector, domain)? What happens
  with an unknown or unsupported country? Can the user switch country mid-flow?
- **Content ownership:** which texts come from Strapi and which are in code (buttons, step
  titles, generic errors)? What if Strapi content is missing or malformed?
- **States:** loading, empty, error (Strapi down, timeout), partial content, retry.
- **Persistence:** what survives a reload or back navigation? When is the stored data cleared
  (after payment? on country switch)? Is anything sensitive persisted?
- **Navigation:** can the user deep-link to step 2 or 3 without completing earlier steps? What
  does browser back do?
- **Concurrency and idempotency:** double clicks, double submits, retries.
- **Draft vs published, active vs inactive:** which combinations are visible?
- **Formatting:** currency, decimals, thousand separators, date format per country.
- **Security and privacy:** masking rules (which characters are shown), what is logged, what
  reaches the browser.
- **Accessibility:** keyboard path, focus on step change and on errors, labels, error announcements.
- **Responsive:** mobile layout of complex parts (plan comparison, summary).
- **Configuration change:** what happens if content changes while a user is mid-flow?
- **Verifiability:** can each criterion be checked by an automated test? If not, why not, and how
  will it be checked manually?

## Quality bar for HC1 (self-check before handing over)

- [ ] Every business rule is refined and covered by ≥ 1 AC.
- [ ] Every AC is observable and testable, with concrete example values.
- [ ] Every gap has a proposed default; nothing is silently assumed.
- [ ] Out-of-scope items are explicit.
- [ ] No contradiction with accepted ADRs; needed ADRs are listed.
- [ ] Each AC has a planned test level (unit / component / e2e / manual).
- [ ] `tasks.md` exists, and every task references ACs.

# AGENTS.md

Catalogue of the AI agents and skills used in this repository.

- **Binding conventions** for every agent are in [CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md). If you use a tool
  other than Claude Code that reads `AGENTS.md`, read `CLAUDE.md` first: it is the single source
  of rules, and this file does not repeat them.
- **The flow** (order, checkpoints, approval criteria) is in [FLOW.md](FLOW.md).

## Subagents (`.claude/agents/`)

Every subagent has `Agent` disallowed (no nested delegation) and a `PreToolUse` hook that
enforces its write scope (`.claude/hooks/enforce-write-scope.mjs`).

| Agent | Model | Flow step | Inputs | Outputs | Allowed tools | Write scope (enforced) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [spec-writer](.claude/agents/spec-writer.md) | Opus 5.5 | 1 Spec | `story.md`, accepted ADRs, `CLAUDE.md` | `spec.md`, `tasks.md` | Read, Grep, Glob, Write, Edit, Skill | `specs/US-NN/spec.md`, `specs/US-NN/tasks.md` |
| [architect](.claude/agents/architect.md) | Opus 5.5 | 2 ADRs, spike write-ups | approved spec (*ADRs needed*), spike results | `adr/NNNN-*.md` (Proposed), `docs/spikes/*` | Read, Grep, Glob, Write, Edit, Bash (read-only use), WebFetch, Skill | `adr/**`, `docs/spikes/**`, `tasks.md` |
| [test-engineer](.claude/agents/test-engineer.md) | Sonnet 5.5 | 3 Tests first | approved spec, accepted ADRs | unit, component and e2e tests (red) | Read, Grep, Glob, Write, Edit, Bash, Skill | `**/*.spec.ts`, `**/*.test.ts`, `frontend/e2e/**`, `frontend/src/testing/**`, `backend/tests/**`, `tasks.md` |
| [strapi-developer](.claude/agents/strapi-developer.md) | Sonnet 5.5 | 4 Implementation, 7 Fixes | approved spec, ADRs, tests | content types, seed, permissions | Read, Grep, Glob, Write, Edit, Bash, Skill | `backend/**` except tests, `docker-compose.yml`, `.env.example`, `tasks.md` |
| [frontend-developer](.claude/agents/frontend-developer.md) | Sonnet 5.5 | 4 Implementation, 7 Fixes, spikes | approved spec, ADRs, red tests | Angular code | Read, Grep, Glob, Write, Edit, Bash, Skill | `frontend/**` except tests, `spikes/**`, `docker-compose.yml`, `.env.example`, `tasks.md` |
| [code-reviewer](.claude/agents/code-reviewer.md) | Opus 5.5 | 6 Review | branch diff, spec, ADRs, previous rounds | review report | Read, Grep, Glob, Write, Bash (verification only), Skill (**no Edit**) | `reviews/US-NN-review-RN.md` |

The main session (Opus 5.5) is the **orchestrator**: it runs the flow, invokes the agents,
checks their diffs, and talks to the human. It does not do the agents' work on stories.

## Skills (`.claude/skills/`)

### 7.1 Field configuration (per country, draft & publish on)

| Attribute | Type | Rules |
|---|---|---|
| `key` | string | Required. `^[a-z][a-zA-Z0-9]*$`. Unique per country. Not shown to users. |
| `label` | string | Required, non-empty. Spanish. |
| `type` | enumeration | `text`, `number`, `select`, `date`, `checkbox`. |
| `isRequired` | boolean | Default `false`. |
| `helpText` | text | Optional. Spanish. |
| `placeholder` | string | Optional. Spanish. Never used instead of a label. |
| `errorMessage` | string | Required. Spanish. Field-level message (US-01-Q-04). |
| `sortOrder` | integer | Required. Ascending; ties by `key`. |
| `options` | list of { `value` string, `label` string, `sortOrder` integer } | Required and non-empty when `type` is `select`; ignored otherwise. `value` unique within the field. |
| `rules` | list of structured rules (below) | Zero or more, in evaluation order. Each may carry an optional `message` (Spanish) that overrides `errorMessage`. |
| `requiredMessage` | string | Optional. Overrides `errorMessage` for the `required` check. |
| country | per multi-country ADR | Exactly one country per field. |

Rule kinds (structured, not free JSON):

| Kind | Parameters | Applies to | Semantics |
|---|---|---|---|
| `minLength` / `maxLength` | `value` integer ≥ 0 | text | Trimmed length, inclusive. |
| `min` / `max` | `value` number | number | Inclusive. |
| `pattern` | `value` ECMAScript regex source, no flags | text | Full match (anchored if not anchored). |
| `minAge` | `years` integer > 0 | date | BR-04. |
| `yearRange` | `maxYearsOld` integer ≥ 0, `maxYearsAhead` integer ≥ 0 | number | BR-03. |
| `rutCheckDigit` | none | text | Modulo-11 check digit, accepts dots/dash and `K`/`k` (subject to US-01-Q-09). |

## FieldConfig contract (v1)

```ts
type FieldType = 'text' | 'number' | 'select' | 'date' | 'checkbox';

interface FieldConfig {
  key: string;              // /^[a-z][a-zA-Z0-9]*$/, unique per country, never shown to users
  type: FieldType;
  label: string;            // Spanish, non-empty
  helpText?: string;
  placeholder?: string;     // never a substitute for the label
  isRequired: boolean;
  sortOrder: number;        // ascending; ties broken by key
  errorMessage: string;     // Spanish, field-level message (US-01-Q-04)
  requiredMessage?: string; // overrides errorMessage for the required check
  options?: SelectOption[]; // required and non-empty when type === 'select'; ignored otherwise
  rules: ValidationRule[];  // evaluation order = config order
}

interface SelectOption { value: string; label: string; sortOrder: number } // value unique per field

type ValidationRule = { message?: string } & (               // message overrides errorMessage
  | { kind: 'minLength' | 'maxLength'; value: number }       // text
  | { kind: 'min' | 'max'; value: number }                   // number
  | { kind: 'pattern'; value: string }                       // text; ECMAScript source, no flags
  | { kind: 'minAge'; years: number }                        // date
  | { kind: 'yearRange'; maxYearsOld: number; maxYearsAhead: number } // number
  | { kind: 'rutCheckDigit' }                                // text (US-01-Q-09)
);
```

**Rule applicability by field type.** A rule on a type it does not apply to is malformed:

| Kind | Applies to |
|---|---|
| `minLength`, `maxLength`, `pattern`, `rutCheckDigit` | `text` |
| `min`, `max`, `yearRange` | `number` |
| `minAge` | `date` |

**Boundary validation (`parseFieldConfigs`).** A field is dropped, with a `console.warn` that
contains no user data, if:
- its `type` is unknown, or its `key` is invalid or duplicated,
- its `label` is empty,
- a `select` has no options, or has duplicated option values,
- a rule is malformed: unknown kind, missing or invalid parameter, or a kind that does not apply
  to the field type,
- a `pattern` does not compile.

A missing `errorMessage` does not drop the field. The fallback message is used instead, with a
warning (see *Error messages*). The exact behaviour for each malformed case is specified in
US-01-Q-18.

# Dynamic form fields

## Scope and precedence

- The **forms library** (Signal Forms or Reactive Forms) is decided by the forms ADR after
  SPIKE-01 (`CLAUDE.md` §7). This skill is **library-agnostic**: it defines the contract and the
  validation semantics that hold whichever API implements them.
- The contract below is **v0**. The US-01 spec may refine it. When it changes, update this
  skill in the same PR.

## Pipeline (each stage is a pure, unit-tested function)

```
Strapi REST response
  → parseFieldConfigs()     boundary validation: unknown or malformed → dropped + warning
  → sort by sortOrder       stable; ties broken by key
  → buildFormModel()        initial values per type
  → buildValidators()       rules → validators (library adapter)
  → render                  one control component per field type
```

Keep the parsing and validation semantics free of Angular so they can be tested without
TestBed. Only the adapter and the rendering touch the forms library.

## FieldConfig contract (v0)

```ts
type FieldType = 'text' | 'number' | 'select' | 'date' | 'checkbox';

interface FieldConfig {
  key: string;              // stable machine key, unique per country (e.g. 'documentNumber')
  type: FieldType;
  label: string;            // Spanish, from Strapi
  helpText?: string;
  placeholder?: string;
  isRequired: boolean;
  sortOrder: number;
  options?: SelectOption[]; // required and non-empty when type === 'select'
  rules: ValidationRule[];
  messages: Partial<Record<RuleKind | 'required', string>>; // Spanish error copy, from Strapi
}

interface SelectOption { value: string; label: string; sortOrder: number }

type RuleKind = 'minLength' | 'maxLength' | 'min' | 'max' | 'pattern' | 'minAge' | 'yearRange';

type ValidationRule =
  | { kind: 'minLength' | 'maxLength'; value: number }
  | { kind: 'min' | 'max'; value: number }
  | { kind: 'pattern'; value: string }                      // ECMAScript regex source, no flags
  | { kind: 'minAge'; years: number }                       // policyholder legal age
  | { kind: 'yearRange'; maxYearsOld: number; maxYearsAhead: number };
```

**Boundary validation (`parseFieldConfigs`).** A field is dropped, with a `console.warn` that
contains no user data, if:
- its `type` is unknown,
- a `select` has no options,
- a rule is malformed,
- a `pattern` does not compile, or
- its `key` is duplicated.

The form must still render with the remaining fields. If **zero** valid fields remain, show
the error state with a retry option, never an empty form that can be submitted.

## Validation semantics (business rules from US-01)

| Rule | Semantics | Boundaries (must be unit-tested) |
|---|---|---|
| `required` | text: non-empty after trim · number: a value is present (0 is a value) · select: a value is chosen · date: a valid date is present · checkbox: `true` | Whitespace-only text is invalid |
| `minAge { years }` | Age in completed years on **today's local date** ≥ `years`. Both CO and CL use 18 per the seed, but the value comes from config. | 18th birthday today → valid; tomorrow → invalid; 29 Feb birthdays |
| `yearRange { maxYearsOld, maxYearsAhead }` | `currentYear − maxYearsOld ≤ year ≤ currentYear + maxYearsAhead`. US-01: 20 years old, 1 ahead. | Both limits inclusive; the year just outside each limit is invalid |
| `min` / `max` | Numeric value bounds, inclusive | |
| `minLength` / `maxLength` | Bounds on trimmed length, inclusive | |
| `pattern` | Full match: anchor with `^…$` if the config does not | |

- "Today" must come from an **injectable clock** (for example an `InjectionToken<() => Date>`),
  so tests can pin the date. Never call `new Date()` directly inside a validator.
- Country-specific checks (RUT check digit, plate formats) are expressed as config rules when a
  pattern is enough. A rule kind that needs code (for example `rutCheckDigit`) is a **spec
  change plus a code change**; flag it in the spec as a gap rather than hard-coding it.

## Error messages

- Show the configured message for the first failing rule, in this priority order: `required`,
  then the order of the rules in config.
- Fallback when a message is missing: a generic Spanish message (`"Revisa este campo."`) and a
  boundary warning. Never show a rule kind or an English text to the user.
- Show errors after the field is touched, or after a submit attempt.

## Accessibility of generated fields

- `<label for>` bound to every control. Checkbox labels are clickable.
- `aria-describedby` points to the help text and to the error element (when the error is shown).
  Use `aria-invalid="true"` on invalid fields and `aria-required` when required.
- The error container uses `role="alert"` or a polite live region. Do not announce every field
  on every keystroke.
- Use native controls (`<input type=number|date|checkbox>`, `<select>`) for free keyboard support.
- On a failed submit, focus the first invalid field in `sortOrder`.

## Persistence (keep data when going back: US-01 AC)

The form value lives in the wizard state store, not in the component. Re-entering step 1
rebuilds the form from config and **hydrates** it from the store. Values for keys that are no
longer configured are dropped.

# Dynamic form fields

## Scope and precedence

- The **forms library** (Signal Forms or Reactive Forms) is decided by the forms ADR after
  SPIKE-01 (`CLAUDE.md` §7). This skill is **library-agnostic**: it defines the contract and the
  validation semantics that hold whichever API implements them.
- The contract below is **v1**, aligned with `specs/US-01/spec.md` §7.1 and §7.3 (refinements
  listed in §7.4, authorised at HC1 by Felipe Sabogal on 2026-11-20, task US-01-T-29). **The spec
  is the source of truth.** If they ever disagree, follow the spec and update this skill in the
  same PR.

## Pipeline (each stage is a pure, unit-tested function)

```
Strapi REST response
  → parseFieldConfigs()     boundary validation: unknown or malformed → dropped + warning
  → sort by sortOrder       stable; ties broken by key
  → buildFormModel()        initial values per type
  → buildValidators()       rules → validators (library adapter)
  → render                  one control component per field type
```

Keep the parsing and validation semantics free of Angular so they can be tested without
TestBed. Only the adapter and the rendering touch the forms library.

## FieldConfig contract (v1)

```ts
type FieldType = 'text' | 'number' | 'select' | 'date' | 'checkbox';

interface FieldConfig {
  key: string;              // /^[a-z][a-zA-Z0-9]*$/, unique per country, never shown to users
  type: FieldType;
  label: string;            // Spanish, non-empty
  helpText?: string;
  placeholder?: string;     // never a substitute for the label
  isRequired: boolean;
  sortOrder: number;        // ascending; ties broken by key
  errorMessage: string;     // Spanish, field-level message (US-01-Q-04)
  requiredMessage?: string; // overrides errorMessage for the required check
  options?: SelectOption[]; // required and non-empty when type === 'select'; ignored otherwise
  rules: ValidationRule[];  // evaluation order = config order
}

interface SelectOption { value: string; label: string; sortOrder: number } // value unique per field

type ValidationRule = { message?: string } & (               // message overrides errorMessage
  | { kind: 'minLength' | 'maxLength'; value: number }       // text
  | { kind: 'min' | 'max'; value: number }                   // number
  | { kind: 'pattern'; value: string }                       // text; ECMAScript source, no flags
  | { kind: 'minAge'; years: number }                        // date
  | { kind: 'yearRange'; maxYearsOld: number; maxYearsAhead: number } // number
  | { kind: 'rutCheckDigit' }                                // text (US-01-Q-09)
);
```

**Rule applicability by field type.** A rule on a type it does not apply to is malformed:

| Kind | Applies to |
|---|---|
| `minLength`, `maxLength`, `pattern`, `rutCheckDigit` | `text` |
| `min`, `max`, `yearRange` | `number` |
| `minAge` | `date` |

**Boundary validation (`parseFieldConfigs`).** A field is dropped, with a `console.warn` that
contains no user data, if:
- its `type` is unknown, or its `key` is invalid or duplicated,
- its `label` is empty,
- a `select` has no options, or has duplicated option values,
- a rule is malformed: unknown kind, missing or invalid parameter, or a kind that does not apply
  to the field type,
- a `pattern` does not compile.

A missing `errorMessage` does not drop the field. The fallback message is used instead, with a
warning (see *Error messages*). The exact behaviour for each malformed case is specified in
US-01-Q-18.

The form must still render with the remaining fields. If **zero** valid fields remain, show
the error state with a retry option, never an empty form that can be submitted.

## Validation semantics (business rules from US-01)

| Rule | Semantics | Boundaries (must be unit-tested) |
|---|---|---|
| `required` | text: non-empty after trim · number: a value is present (0 is a value) · select: a value is chosen · date: a valid date is present · checkbox: `true` | Whitespace-only text is invalid |
| `minAge { years }` | Age in completed years on **today's local date** ≥ `years`. Both CO and CL use 18 per the seed, but the value comes from config. | 18th birthday today → valid; tomorrow → invalid; 29 Feb birthdays |
| `yearRange { maxYearsOld, maxYearsAhead }` | `currentYear − maxYearsOld ≤ year ≤ currentYear + maxYearsAhead`. US-01: 20 years old, 1 ahead. | Both limits inclusive; the year just outside each limit is invalid |
| `min` / `max` | Numeric value bounds, inclusive | |
| `minLength` / `maxLength` | Bounds on trimmed length, inclusive | |
| `pattern` | Full match: anchor with `^…$` if the config does not | |

- "Today" must come from an **injectable clock** (for example an `InjectionToken<() => Date>`),
  so tests can pin the date. Never call `new Date()` directly inside a validator.
- Country-specific checks (RUT check digit, plate formats) are expressed as config rules when a
  pattern is enough. A rule kind that needs code (for example `rutCheckDigit`) is a **spec
  change plus a code change**; flag it in the spec as a gap rather than hard-coding it.

## Error messages

- Show the configured message for the first failing rule, in this priority order: `required`,
  then the order of the rules in config.
- Fallback when a message is missing: a generic Spanish message (`"Revisa este campo."`) and a
  boundary warning. Never show a rule kind or an English text to the user.
- Show errors after the field is touched, or after a submit attempt.

## Accessibility of generated fields

- `<label for>` bound to every control. Checkbox labels are clickable.
- `aria-describedby` points to the help text and to the error element (when the error is shown).
  Use `aria-invalid="true"` on invalid fields and `aria-required` when required.
- The error container uses `role="alert"` or a polite live region. Do not announce every field
  on every keystroke.
- Use native controls (`<input type=number|date|checkbox>`, `<select>`) for free keyboard support.
- On a failed submit, focus the first invalid field in `sortOrder`.

## Persistence (keep data when going back: US-01 AC)

The form value lives in the wizard state store, not in the component. Re-entering step 1
rebuilds the form from config and **hydrates** it from the store. Values for keys that are no
longer configured are dropped.

## FieldConfig contract (v1)

```ts
type FieldType = 'text' | 'number' | 'select' | 'date' | 'checkbox';

interface FieldConfig {
  key: string;              // /^[a-z][a-zA-Z0-9]*$/, unique per country, never shown to users
  type: FieldType;
  label: string;            // Spanish, non-empty
  helpText?: string;
  placeholder?: string;     // never a substitute for the label
  isRequired: boolean;
  sortOrder: number;        // ascending; ties broken by key
  errorMessage: string;     // Spanish, field-level message (US-01-Q-04)
  requiredMessage?: string; // overrides errorMessage for the required check
  options?: SelectOption[]; // required and non-empty when type === 'select'; ignored otherwise
  rules: ValidationRule[];  // evaluation order = config order
}

interface SelectOption { value: string; label: string; sortOrder: number } // value unique per field

type ValidationRule = { message?: string } & (               // message overrides errorMessage
  | { kind: 'minLength' | 'maxLength'; value: number }       // text
  | { kind: 'min' | 'max'; value: number }                   // number
  | { kind: 'pattern'; value: string }                       // text; ECMAScript source, no flags
  | { kind: 'minAge'; years: number }                        // date
  | { kind: 'yearRange'; maxYearsOld: number; maxYearsAhead: number } // number
  | { kind: 'rutCheckDigit' }                                // text (US-01-Q-09)
);
```

**Rule applicability by field type.** A rule on a type it does not apply to is malformed:

| Kind | Applies to |
|---|---|
| `minLength`, `maxLength`, `pattern`, `rutCheckDigit` | `text` |
| `min`, `max`, `yearRange` | `number` |
| `minAge` | `date` |

**Boundary validation (`parseFieldConfigs`).** A field is dropped, with a `console.warn` that
contains no user data, if:
- its `type` is unknown, or its `key` is invalid or duplicated,
- its `label` is empty,
- a `select` has no options, or has duplicated option values,
- a rule is malformed: unknown kind, missing or invalid parameter, or a kind that does not apply
  to the field type,
- a `pattern` does not compile.

A missing `errorMessage` does not drop the field. The fallback message is used instead, with a
warning (see *Error messages*). The exact behaviour for each malformed case is specified in
US-01-Q-18.

## Decisions and the strongest argument against each

**ADR-0001: multi-country content strategy and country context.** Chosen: option A (a `country` collection type, plus a required `manyToOne` `country` relation on `form-field`, `plan` and `terms`) and R1 (the country in the URL path).
- **Strapi side:**
  - A `country` entry holds `code`, `name`, `currencyCode`, `locale` and `sortOrder`.
  - `config/api.ts` sets `documents.strictRelations: true`, so Strapi refuses to publish an item with no country.
  - `key` uniqueness per country is enforced by a Document Service middleware, because Strapi's `unique` is global.
- **Angular side:**
  - The list of supported countries comes from Strapi (published `country` entries), loaded once per page load. There are no country literals in code.
  - `/` shows a chooser. `/ar/...` shows "Este país no está disponible." with links to each country. If the country list cannot be loaded, an error with "Reintentar" is shown instead, so the app never wrongly says a country is unavailable.
  - Entering another country's context discards the stored data (Q-02).
- **Routing (T-06 folded in):**
  - Routes are `/:country/datos`, `/:country/planes` and `/:country/resumen`.
  - `planes` has `children: []` and no component, guarded by `wizardStepGuard` (a `CanActivateFn`).
  - When step 1 data is missing or invalid, the guard sends the user back to `/<country>/datos` with `RedirectCommand` and `replaceUrl`, so the blocked address does not stay in history.
  - Step slugs are Spanish because users see them.
- **Strongest argument against:** option B (i18n locales `es-CO`/`es-CL`) gives per-country uniqueness for free (Strapi's unique check is scoped by locale, verified) and lets editors copy one country's content to another. Option A needs custom code for uniqueness and has no copy tool. The country list being content also means the chooser and the unknown-country page now depend on Strapi being reachable.

**ADR-0002: Strapi access and security.** Chosen: option 2, a same-origin nginx proxy plus the Strapi public role.
- **Proxy and front-end build:**
  - nginx serves the Angular build and proxies only GET requests on allow-listed `/api/` paths.
  - It sends `Cache-Control: no-store` on API responses and rejects any `Authorization` header.
  - The build uses the relative path `/api`, so no runtime config file is needed. The upstream address is set through the nginx image's env templates.
- **Public role:** exactly `find` on `country` and `form-field`, with no `findOne`. The users-permissions defaults on the public role (`auth.register` and others) are removed and `allow_register` is set to false.
- **Strapi hardening:**
  - A global middleware forces published content on anonymous reads.
  - CORS is closed to an env-driven allow-list.
  - The default "Full Access" token is deleted.
- **AC-03 test writes:** the Playwright Node process logs in to the admin API with fictitious dev admin credentials, which bootstrap creates from env vars. It creates a `custom` token scoped to form-field create/delete, POSTs directly to Strapi's port (a REST POST publishes by default), then deletes the field and the token.
- **Strongest argument against:** Strapi's own port (open for the admin panel) still answers the public `find` endpoints and skips the proxy's allow-list. Option 3 (proxy-injected token, empty public role) would close that port to anonymous reads.

  - On reading, the entry is checked first; values for removed fields or options are dropped (AC-23).
- **Clearing:** on tab close (the browser does it), on switching country, and on successful payment (US-03's job). It is not cleared on a rejected payment.
- **Privacy:** values are never logged, sent or put in the URL. There is no client-side encryption, because the key would sit next to the data. If storage is unavailable, the store falls back to memory.
- **Strongest argument against:** the document number and birth date stay in clear text in tab storage while the tab is open, readable by any script on the origin.   - **Signal Forms, static model** `signal({vehicleYear:'', acceptsOffers:false})`:
    - `f.vehicleYear().value()` is `string`.
    - `f.nope` and `.value.set(2020)` are compile errors.
  - **Signal Forms, runtime model** `signal<Record<string, string|boolean>>`:

    - number: `Type 'RawValue' is not assignable to type 'string | number | null'`
    - date: `Type 'RawValue' is not assignable to type 'string | number | Date | null'`
    - `FieldTree<string|boolean>` is not assignable to `FieldTree<string>` (a `@ts-expect-error` holds).

  | Piece | Lines |
  |---|---|
  | Shared core (`core/*.ts`) | 209 (clock 4, field-config 32, form-values 32, parse 83, validate 58) |
  | Signal Forms component (`.ts` 69 + `.html` 42) | 111 |
  | Reactive Forms component (`.ts` 72 + `.html` 40) | 112 |
  | Tests (criteria 152, core 82, typing 74, library-facts 60, harness 67) | 435 |
  | Fixture JSON | 57 |

  - Signal Forms has 2 cast helpers, an `untracked` wrapper, and `FormRoot` with `submission` options.
  - Reactive Forms has `normalise()`, an explicit `markAllAsTouched()`, and a DOM lookup for focus.

  `npx ng build` and `npx ng test --watch=false --reporters=verbose` both succeed: 4 files, 38/38 pass.
  
  | Suite | Pass/Total |
  |---|---|
  | `[signal-forms]` criteria a-j | 11/11 |
  | `[reactive-forms]` criteria a-j | 11/11 |
  | core | 8/8 |
  | typing | 4/4 |
  | library facts | 4/4 |
  
  Sensitivity check: removing `focusBoundControl()` failed `[signal-forms] (i)`, and removing `markAllAsTouched()` failed `[reactive-forms] (h)`. Both were restored.
  
  ## Open questions / unverified
  
  1. All runs were in jsdom. Not verified in a real browser: focus and scroll behaviour, native `date` and `number` UI, `badInput` handling (`NativeInputParseError` is in the source but was not exercised), mobile keyboards, and screen reader announcements of `role="alert"`.
  2. Blur was simulated with `new FocusEvent('blur')` and typing with `input` plus `change` events. Real event ordering is not covered.
  3. Forcing a string model in Reactive Forms with `DefaultValueAccessor` (for example `type="text" inputmode="numeric"`, or a custom accessor) was not tried.
  4. `rutCheckDigit` is not implemented.
  5. Output for an unchecked optional checkbox is `false` in the spike. The spec must say `false` or `null`.
  6. A config change while mounted rebuilds the form from `stored` in both libraries, so values typed since mount are lost. Whether step 1 can change config while mounted (a country switch) is a spec question.
  7. Async validators and `submit({ ignoreValidators })` were not exercised.
  8. A dynamic `[type]` binding together with `[formField]` was avoided (static `@switch` branches), so it is unverified.
  9. Bundle size, performance with many fields, and SSR were not measured.
  10. Error visibility is hand-built in both (`touched && invalid`). `provideSignalFormsConfig` (class and ARIA auto-binding) was not explored.
  11. The vendored `signal-forms.md` forbids `null` in the model. The spike confirms that a non-null model with `null` only in the mapped output works. It also shows `null` can still appear at runtime in a `number` model through native inputs (row a).

## Environment

|---|---|
| Node | 24.22.1 |
| Scaffold | `npx @angular/cli@22.3.0 new spike-01-forms --directory spikes/spike-01-forms --skip-git --ssr=false --style=css --skip-install --defaults` |

| TypeScript | 6.0.3 |
| Vitest | 5.1.1 (`ng test`, `@angular/build:unit-test`) |
| DOM | jsdom 31 (no real browser) |
| tsconfig | CLI default has no `strict`. The spike adds `strict: true` and `resolveJsonModule: true`. `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` is off. |
| Change detection | zoneless (CLI default) |

- `ng build` hung with no output until `NG_CLI_ANALYTICS=false CI=1` were set (an interactive prompt).

API facts were read from the installed `node_modules/@angular/forms/types/_structure-chunk.d.ts` and `signals.d.ts`, and from the compiled `fesm2022/*.mjs`. - Pure functions, with no Angular import except the `CLOCK` token (`InjectionToken<() => Date>`).
- The functions are `parseFieldConfigs`, `validateField(cfg, value, today)`, `hydrate`, `toOutput`, `parseIsoDate` and `ageOn`.
- `validateField` applies required, the optional-empty skip, integer-only, then the rules in config order. The first failing message wins.
- Both adapters call the same `validateField` from one custom validator per field.
- The spike did not exercise the built-in validators (`required()`, `min()`, `pattern()` / `Validators.*`).

| # | Criterion | Signal Forms (`@angular/forms/signals`) | Reactive Forms (`FormRecord`) |

Test: `[signal-forms] (a)`. | Works after a workaround. `NumberValueAccessor` (selected by `input[type=number][formControl]`) writes `number\|null` into the control even when it is declared `FormControl<string\|boolean>`. Not tried: forcing `DefaultValueAccessor`. Tests: `[reactive-forms] (a)`, `(e)`, and `library-facts.spec.ts`. |
| b | Empty date: required vs optional; empty optional valid and skips `minAge` | Works. Date held as `''` / ISO string. `<input type="date">` with a string model falls through to `element.value`. Optional empty is valid and the rule is skipped. Once filled, the rule runs. Test: `[signal-forms] (b)`. | Works, same behaviour. `DefaultValueAccessor` handles `type=date` as a string. Test: `[reactive-forms] (b)`. |

The value is the union, and the union does not compile against native controls (see Typing). Needed a cast helper. Tests: `typing.spec.ts`, `[signal-forms] (e)`. | Static `FormGroup`: precise. Typing alone does not touch. After a failed submit there are 3 alerts (birthDate, make, vehicleYear) and the optional fields stay quiet. `aria-invalid` and `aria-describedby` are bound. The model keeps what was typed (`'   '` stays in the model, the output is `null`). Test: `[signal-forms] (j)`. | Works with the same `toOutput()`, after the `normalise()` workaround from (a). ## Typing observations

- **Signal Forms, static model** `signal({vehicleYear:'', acceptsOffers:false})`: `f.vehicleYear().value()` is `string`; `f.nope` and `.value.set(2020)` are compile errors.
- **Signal Forms, runtime model** `signal<Record<string, string|boolean>>`: `f['anything']` compiles as `FieldTree<string|boolean>`; at runtime an unknown key throws `TypeError: f.<key> is not a function`.
- **Signal Forms, template binding of the union does not compile.** Captured `ng build` errors: text → `TS2322: Type 'WritableSignal<RawValue>' is not assignable to type '{ (): string; set: (v: string) => void; } | { (): number | null; set: (v: number | null) => void; }'`; checkbox → `Type 'RawValue' is not assignable to type 'boolean'`; number → `Type 'RawValue' is not assignable to type 'string | number | null'`; date → `Type 'RawValue' is not assignable to type 'string | number | Date | null'`. `FieldTree<string|boolean>` is not assignable to `FieldTree<string>` (`@ts-expect-error` holds). Workaround used: `str(key)` / `bool(key)` accessors doing `as unknown as FieldTree<string>` / `FieldTree<boolean>` (2 casts).
- Native control accepted types in Signal Forms: text → `string`; number → `string|number|null`; date → `string|number|Date|null`; checkbox → `boolean`.
- **Reactive Forms, `FormRecord<FormControl<string|boolean>>`:** `controls[key]` is `FormControl<string|boolean>` (no `undefined` because `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` is off); `get(key)` is nullable; `setValue(5)` is a compile error; the template `[formControl]` binding compiles with no casts.
- **Both:** the types describe the model, not what native controls write at runtime (`null` from cleared number inputs).
- **`form()` inside `computed()`** throws `NG0602: effect() cannot be called from within a reactive context` (`form()` creates an effect). The adapter wraps it in `untracked(() => form(...))`. Building a `FormRecord` inside `computed()` had no such issue.
- `form()` needs an injection context or `{ injector }` in its options.

content.text:
Los cuatro ADRs tienen la sección de *Consequences* con varias contras ("Bad, because…", entre 11 y 18 por ADR). Lo que falta es el **argumento más fuerte en contra como tal**: el architect lo escribió en sus reportes, no en los ADRs. Lo dejo como hallazgo mío para HC2.

Todo lo demás está bien:
- El architect solo tocó `adr/`, `docs/spikes/` y `tasks.md`, y la spec no cambió.
- Los cuatro ADRs están en `Proposed`, con 3 o 4 opciones cada uno.
- El escaneo de secretos sale limpio.

Ya puedes hacer **HC2: aceptación de los ADRs 0001–0004**.

## Los 4 ADRs

| ADR | Decisión propuesta | Argumento más fuerte en contra (según el architect) |
|---|---|---|
| **0001 Multi-país** | En Strapi, una colección `country` (código, moneda, locale) y una relación obligatoria hacia campos, planes y términos. En Angular, el país va en la URL (`/:country/datos`, `/planes`, `/resumen`); la lista de países viene de Strapi; `/` muestra un selector y un país desconocido muestra el mensaje de "no disponible". El paso 2 es una ruta vacía con su guard, y cambiar de país borra los datos. | Con i18n (un locale por país), la unicidad de la clave por país vendría gratis y los editores podrían copiar contenido de un país a otro. La opción elegida necesita código propio para la unicidad, y el selector depende de que Strapi responda. |
| **0002 Seguridad** | Un proxy nginx en el mismo origen que solo deja pasar GET a rutas permitidas de `/api/`, con `no-store` y rechazando `Authorization`. El rol público solo tiene `find` sobre `country` y `form-field`. Además: un middleware que fuerza contenido publicado, CORS cerrado, se borra el token "Full Access" y se desactiva el registro. El e2e de AC-03 crea un token temporal con credenciales de admin de desarrollo ficticias. | El puerto propio de Strapi, abierto para el panel de admin, también responde los `find` públicos y se salta el proxy. Ocultar los borradores ahí depende de un middleware propio que una actualización de Strapi podría romper sin avisar. La opción 3 (el proxy inyecta el token y el rol público queda vacío) cerraría ese hueco. |
| **0003 Persistencia** | `sessionStorage` en una sola clave versionada, de la que solo es dueño el `QuoteStore`. No guarda la configuración, solo los valores, y al leer descarta los campos que ya no existen. Se borra al cerrar la pestaña, al cambiar de país y tras pagar. Sin cifrado, porque la clave viviría junto a los datos. | El documento y la fecha de nacimiento quedan en claro mientras la pestaña está abierta, y un navegador que restaura la sesión los recupera. La opción de guardar solo en memoria lo evita, a cambio de perder los datos al recargar. |
| **0004 Formularios** | Signal Forms sobre una capa de validación propia que no depende de la librería. El modelo no admite `null`: los números se guardan como texto y se convierten al salir. Para el foco en el primer error usa `focusBoundControl()`, y solo se permiten 2 casts en plantillas. | Solo lleva 5,5 meses como API estable (con 39 cambios en `forms` desde 22.0), toda la evidencia del spike viene de jsdom, y con un modelo construido en tiempo de ejecución pierde la ventaja de tipado. Mitigación: cambiar de librería costaría reescribir un componente de unas 110 líneas. |

## Puntos donde los ADRs obligan a ajustar la spec aprobada (10)

1. **§7.3:** el país deja de ser `'CO' | 'CL'` y pasa a ser un código ISO validado contra la lista que llega de Strapi.
2. **§8:** falta el estado "no se pudo cargar la lista de países", con su texto.
3. **ADR-0002** añade una comprobación de seguridad que ningún AC cubre: una petición anónima con `?status=draft` no debe devolver borradores, y un POST tiene que recibir 405. ¿Se crea un AC nuevo, o queda como comprobación sin trazar?
4. **ADR-0002** añade al bootstrap: el admin de desarrollo, el borrado del token por defecto, el registro desactivado, el middleware y CORS. Hay que re-asignar T-18, T-19 y T-20.
5. AC-21 se mantiene tal cual. Solo es información, no requiere cambio.
6. AC-17 pasa a tener un archivo de test unitario con nombre propio.
7. **Un checkbox opcional sin marcar**, ¿se guarda como `false` o como `null`? El architect recomienda `false`.
8. Un cambio de configuración con el formulario montado no requiere cambiar la spec.
9. **Conflicto entre ADR-0003 y §7.3:** el store guarda en cada cambio, pero un valor a medio escribir como `2015.5` no cabe como entero. Las alternativas: guardar el valor crudo mientras se edita, o aplicar la forma de §7.3 solo al pulsar "Continuar".
10. Un número que no se puede interpretar se lee como vacío y muestra el mensaje de "obligatorio" en lugar del de formato. ¿Es aceptable para AC-09?

## Mis hallazgos como orquestador

- **H1:** como dije arriba, el argumento más fuerte en contra no aparece en los ADRs, aunque FLOW.md lo pide para HC2. Propongo añadir una sección *Strongest argument against* a la plantilla `adr-madr` y a los cuatro ADRs.
- **H2:** en el primer lote, el architect editó `tasks.md` vía Bash. Él mismo lo declaró y lo confirmé con el diff. En el segundo lote usó Edit, como le pedí. Lo registraré en FLOW.md como el límite conocido observado en la práctica.
- **H3:** el ADR-0004 contradice a la skill de Angular ("usa 0 para números"). Está bien según la regla de precedencia, pero conviene que lo sepas.

## Cómo responder

Para cada ADR: **Accepted**, **Rejected** o cambios. Para los puntos 1–4, 7, 9 y 10, tu decisión. Para H1, si lo apruebas. Si alguno de los puntos cambia la spec, el `spec-writer` hace la v0.3 (solo toca `spec.md`) y la vuelves a ver en HC1. Nada se commitea hasta tu decisión.

# ADRs (MADR 4)

## When a decision deserves an ADR

Write one if **any** of these is true:

- It affects more than one user story or more than one layer (Angular + Strapi).
- It is expensive to reverse (data model, content strategy, state management, security model).
- There were at least two reasonable options, and someone could later ask "why this one?".
- It overrides guidance from a third-party skill or a framework default.

Do **not** write an ADR for local implementation details that the spec or code review covers.

## Rules

- File: `adr/NNNN-kebab-title.md`, 4-digit sequential number. Never reuse a number. Use the
  template in [templates/adr.md](templates/adr.md).
- **At least two real alternatives**, each with honest pros and cons. A strawman option
  ("do nothing" with no merit) does not count as an alternative.
- Decision drivers must trace back to requirements: the assessment PDF, a spec `BR`/`AC`, or
  `CLAUDE.md`.
- Consequences include the **bad** ones and how they are mitigated.
- *Confirmation* says how compliance is checked: a test, a review checklist item, a script.
- Facts about libraries (versions, API stability) must be verified against the official source
  or the installed package, with a link or version. Never state them from memory.
- If a spike informed the decision, link its findings (the branch is not merged; summarise the
  results in the ADR).

## Lifecycle (the status changes only by these rules)

| Status | Who sets it | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `Proposed` | architect subagent | Ready for HC2. Not binding. |
| `Accepted` | **human only** | Binding (precedence level 2 in `CLAUDE.md`). Record `Decided by` and date. |
| `Rejected` | **human only** | Kept in the repo, with the reason. |
| `Superseded by ADR-NNNN` | architect, after the new ADR is accepted | Old file kept, with a link to the replacement. |

Accepted ADRs are never rewritten. A change of mind means a new ADR that supersedes the old one.

## Index

Keep `adr/README.md` updated: number, title, status, date, related stories.
